artists.name: Caetano Veloso
artists.summary: Brazilian singer and songwriter who co-led the Tropicália movement. He mixed bossa nova, rock and poetry, and remains one of Brazil's most important artists.
know: He co-founded Tropicália with Gilberto Gil in 1967 and 1968.
The military dictatorship jailed him in 1968 and he spent 1969 to 1972 in exile in London.
He wrote a memoir about the period called Verdade Tropical (1997).

influencedBy.why: Veloso has said hearing João Gilberto as a teenager set the course of his life in music.
Tropicália openly borrowed the studio experiments and pop-art attitude of the late Beatles.
His harmonic language grew out of Jobim's bossa nova songwriting.

cousins.why: A poet-songwriter who changed what popular lyrics could do.
A restless songwriter who kept reinventing her style.

artists.name: Os Mutantes
artists.summary: Brazilian psychedelic rock band formed by Arnaldo and Sérgio Dias Baptista with Rita Lee. Their playful, experimental records were the rock wing of Tropicália.
know: They played on the 1968 manifesto album Tropicália ou Panis et Circencis.
Kurt Cobain was a fan and urged them to reunite in the 1990s.
They reunited in 2006 with a concert at London's Barbican.
keyAlbums: A Divina Comédia ou Ando Meio Desligado

influencedBy.why: Their studio tricks and sound collage borrowed heavily from the psychedelic Beatles.
They worked as Veloso's backing band and took on Tropicália's mix of Brazilian music and rock.

cousins.why: Early psychedelic studio experimenters.
Melodic, baroque psychedelic pop.

artists.name: Weather Report
artists.summary: A fusion band led by Joe Zawinul and Wayne Shorter that blended jazz improvisation, synthesizers and global rhythms.
know: Founders Zawinul and Shorter had both played on Miles Davis's early electric records.
Bassist Jaco Pastorius joined in the mid 1970s and became a star in the band.
Their tune Birdland was a crossover hit covered by many artists.

influencedBy.why: Founders Zawinul and Shorter played on In a Silent Way and Bitches Brew before forming the band.

cousins.why: A band that fused rock with sophisticated jazz harmony and top session players.
A group that built long, virtuosic, keyboard-rich instrumental pieces.

artists.name: Willie Nelson
artists.summary: Songwriter and singer who wrote hits for others in Nashville, then led the outlaw country movement from Texas. His jazzy phrasing and battered guitar Trigger are instantly recognizable.
know: He wrote "Crazy" for Patsy Cline and "Hello Walls" for Faron Young.
He co-founded Farm Aid in 1985.
His Martin guitar is named Trigger.
songs: Blue Eyes Crying in the Rain

influencedBy.why: He has called Django Reinhardt his favorite guitarist, and his solos borrow from Gypsy jazz.
He has said Sinatra taught him phrasing and recorded the tribute My Way in 2018.
He recorded a full tribute album, To Lefty from Willie, in 1977.
He grew up on Bob Wills and later recorded a western swing album with Asleep at the Wheel.
He has often named Williams as a key songwriting influence.
He admired Ray Charles' blend of country and soul, and they duetted on "Seven Spanish Angels."

cousins.why: A laid-back elder statesman beloved across generations.
A relaxed icon whose persona outgrew his genre.

artists.name: Waylon Jennings
artists.summary: Leader of the 1970s outlaw country movement, who fought Nashville for creative control and played a harder, rock-driven sound.
know: He gave up his seat on Buddy Holly's plane in February 1959, the night of the fatal crash.
Wanted! The Outlaws (1976) was the first country album certified platinum.
He narrated and sang the theme for The Dukes of Hazzard.
songs: Mammas Don't Let Your Babies Grow Up to Be Cowboys
Are You Sure Hank Done It This Way
Bob Wills Is Still the King

influencedBy.why: Holly produced his first single and hired him to play bass.
He held Williams up as the standard in "Are You Sure Hank Done It This Way."
He paid tribute in "Bob Wills Is Still the King."
He and Cash shared an apartment in the mid 1960s and stayed close friends.

cousins.why: Hard-living Southern rebels who did things their own way.
Loud, defiant road dogs who ignored the industry.

artists.name: Emmylou Harris
artists.summary: Singer with a pure, haunting voice who carried Gram Parsons' country rock vision forward and became a central figure in Americana. She is also one of music's most sought-after harmony singers.
know: She was Gram Parsons' duet partner on GP and Grievous Angel.
She made the Trio album with Dolly Parton and Linda Ronstadt in 1987.
Her 1995 album Wrecking Ball, produced by Daniel Lanois, moved her into atmospheric rock.
songs: If I Could Only Win Your Love

influencedBy.why: Parsons was her mentor and duet partner, and she wrote "Boulder to Birmingham" after his death.
She began as a folk singer in the Baez mold.
She took Owens' "Together Again" to number one in 1976.
She had a hit with Dolly's "To Daddy" in 1977.

cousins.why: A gentle, pure voice that blends genres.
A trusted collaborator at the center of her scene.

artists.name: James Taylor
artists.summary: Gentle-voiced singer-songwriter whose personal songs helped launch the 1970s singer-songwriter era.
know: He was the first artist signed to the Beatles' Apple Records, in 1968.
His version of Carole King's "You've Got a Friend" went to number one in 1971.
He was married to singer Carly Simon from 1972 to 1983.
keyAlbums: Mud Slide Slim and the Blue Horizon

influencedBy.why: He signed to their Apple label, and their melodic songwriting shaped his early work.
He has named Ray Charles as a key influence on his singing.
He recorded her "You've Got a Friend" and toured with her.
He had a hit with "How Sweet It Is (To Be Loved by You)", first a Marvin Gaye record.

cousins.why: Warm, simple songs about everyday feelings.
A gentle, personal songwriter of the same era.

artists.name: Cat Stevens
artists.summary: English singer-songwriter of gentle, spiritual songs like "Father and Son" and "Wild World." He left music for decades after converting to Islam and later returned as Yusuf.
know: He converted to Islam in 1977, took the name Yusuf Islam, and stepped away from pop music.
A bout of tuberculosis in 1969 led him to a quieter, more reflective style.
His songs fill the soundtrack of the 1971 film Harold and Maude.
songs: The First Cut Is the Deepest

influencedBy.why: He has said the Beatles inspired him to write his own songs.

cousins.why: Warm, simple, sincere songs.
An acoustic singer-songwriter with broad pop appeal.

artists.name: John Prine
artists.summary: Songwriter known for funny, tender and sharply observed songs about ordinary people. Other songwriters regard him as one of the best ever.
know: He was a mail carrier in Chicago when he started writing songs.
Kris Kristofferson helped launch his career after seeing him in a Chicago club.
He died of COVID-19 complications in April 2020.

influencedBy.why: He often named Hank Williams as a formative influence.
Dylan showed him that folk songs could be personal and literary, and Dylan later praised his songs.
He admired Cash, who covered his songs and championed him.

cousins.why: A master storyteller with humor and detail.
Plainspoken songs about ordinary people.

artists.name: Townes Van Zandt
artists.summary: Texas songwriter of bleak, beautiful songs who was little known in his life but is revered by other writers.
know: Willie Nelson and Merle Haggard took his "Pancho and Lefty" to number one in 1983.
He died on January 1, 1997, the same date Hank Williams died.
His 1977 live album Live at the Old Quarter is considered his essential record.
keyAlbums: The Late Great Townes Van Zandt
Live at the Old Quarter, Houston, Texas

influencedBy.why: He named Hank Williams as one of his great influences.
Seeing Elvis on TV made him want a guitar.
Dylan's songwriting showed him a path into serious folk writing.

cousins.why: Haunting, bleak songs from a revered cult figure.
A cult artist whose legend grew after his death.

artists.name: Black Sabbath
artists.summary: Black Sabbath slowed blues rock down, tuned it lower and built songs on heavy, ominous riffs, creating the template that nearly every later metal style grew from.
know: Tony Iommi's down-tuned, slack-string guitar sound became a core part of the heavy metal tone.
Their self-titled debut was recorded in roughly a single day in 1970.
The band was inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame in 2006.

influencedBy.why: Cream's loud, riff-driven power trio blues was the model the members started from, and Geezer Butler has named Jack Bruce as his key bass influence.
Ozzy Osbourne repeatedly credited the Beatles with making him want to sing in a band, and their melodic sense shaped his vocal lines.
Hendrix's heavy, distorted electric blues showed the band how far amplified guitar riffs could be pushed.
Iommi has said hearing Reinhardt play brilliantly with an injured hand convinced him he could keep playing guitar and adapt his technique.

cousins.why: Raw, slow, primal riffing that laid the groundwork for a whole heavier branch of rock.
Brooding, minor-key sound that set the dark mood for a whole genre that followed.

artists.name: Deep Purple
artists.summary: Deep Purple paired Ritchie Blackmore's guitar with Jon Lord's distorted Hammond organ to help invent hard rock and heavy metal. Smoke on the Water has one of the best-known riffs ever.
know: Smoke on the Water describes a fire at the Montreux Casino during a Frank Zappa concert in 1971.
The Guinness Book once listed them as the world's loudest band.
Their first U.S. hit was a cover of Joe South's Hush.

influencedBy.why: Ritchie Blackmore cited Hendrix's showmanship and volume as a turning point for him.
They covered the Beatles' Help! on their first album.
Singer Ian Gillan named Elvis as his first vocal hero.
Their heavy, jam-stretched blues-rock follows the path Cream opened.

cousins.why: Both put a driving Hammond organ at the center of the band.
Both are British bands built on galloping riffs and dueling solos.

artists.name: The Allman Brothers Band
artists.summary: The Allman Brothers Band mixed blues, jazz and country into long, twin-guitar jams. Duane Allman's slide guitar and Gregg Allman's voice made them the founders of Southern rock.
know: At Fillmore East is often called the greatest live rock album.
Duane Allman died in a motorcycle crash in 1971 at 24.
They used two drummers, Butch Trucks and Jaimoe.

influencedBy.why: Duane Allman said he played Kind of Blue constantly, and the band's modal jams come from it.
Duane Allman named Coltrane's My Favorite Things as a model for their long improvisations.
They covered Elmore James's Done Somebody Wrong at Fillmore East.
They covered Muddy Waters's Trouble No More on their debut.
Their live Stormy Monday is a cover of T-Bone Walker's song.
Duane and Gregg named B.B. King as an early influence after seeing him live.
Gregg Allman cited Ray Charles as a model for his organ and vocals.
They shared bills with the Grateful Dead and followed their two-drummer, long-jam format.

cousins.why: Both carry a soulful Southern voice over blues-rooted music.
Both put the American South at the center of their genre.

artists.name: Lynyrd Skynyrd
artists.summary: Lynyrd Skynyrd brought a three-guitar attack and Ronnie Van Zant's plainspoken songs to Southern rock. Free Bird and Sweet Home Alabama are among the most-played rock songs on radio.
know: The name mocks Leonard Skinner, a gym teacher who punished students for long hair.
Van Zant and two other members died in a 1977 plane crash.
Sweet Home Alabama answers Neil Young's Southern Man.

influencedBy.why: They followed the Allman Brothers' blend of blues, country and dual guitars out of Jacksonville.
Their swaggering boogie-rock owes a lot to the Rolling Stones.
They covered Jimmie Rodgers's T for Texas.
Ronnie Van Zant was a Merle Haggard fan and the band recorded Haggard's Honky Tonk Night Time Man.
Van Zant was a Neil Young fan and wrote Sweet Home Alabama as a reply to Young's Southern Man.
Their live Crossroads follows Cream's arrangement.
Guitarists Allen Collins and Gary Rossington named Eric Clapton as an early model.

cousins.why: Both play tough, outlaw music about Southern working life.
Both carry Southern rock grit and hard-country storytelling.

artists.name: David Bowie
artists.summary: David Bowie reinvented himself through a run of characters and styles, from Ziggy Stardust to Berlin-era electronic rock. He showed rock could be theater and art, and kept experimenting until his last album.
know: Blackstar was released two days before his death in 2016.
He made three albums with Brian Eno, often called the Berlin trilogy.
His eyes looked different colors because of a permanently dilated pupil from a teenage fight.
keyAlbums: The Rise and Fall of Ziggy Stardust and the Spiders from Mars

influencedBy.why: Bowie said seeing Little Richard as a child made him want to play saxophone and be a star.
Bowie, who shared Elvis's birthday, named him as a childhood idol.
He covered I'm Waiting for the Man and produced Lou Reed's Transformer.
He wrote Song for Bob Dylan on Hunky Dory.
He mixed the Stooges' Raw Power and worked closely with Iggy Pop.
He named the song V-2 Schneider after Kraftwerk's Florian Schneider and cited them for the Berlin albums.
Eno co-created Low, Heroes and Lodger with him.
He covered the Kinks' Where Have All the Good Times Gone on Pin Ups.
He covered the Yardbirds' Shapes of Things and I Wish You Would on Pin Ups.
He covered See Emily Play on Pin Ups and cited Syd Barrett as an influence.
He covered I Can't Explain and Anyway, Anyhow, Anywhere on Pin Ups.
He co-wrote Fame with John Lennon and covered Across the Universe.
His friend and rival Marc Bolan helped set the glam style Bowie took further.

cousins.why: Both were genre-hopping shape-shifters who blurred gender and style.
Both treat pop as theater, with personas and costumes.

artists.name: T. Rex
artists.summary: T. Rex, led by Marc Bolan, went from hippie folk duo to the band that launched glam rock in Britain. Hits like Get It On made Bolan a teen idol in the early 1970s.
know: Bolan's glitter-under-the-eyes TV appearance in 1971 is often called the start of glam rock.
Get It On was retitled Bang a Gong (Get It On) in the U.S.
Bolan died in a car crash in 1977, two weeks before his 30th birthday.

influencedBy.why: Bolan ended Get It On with a line from Chuck Berry's Little Queenie as a nod to Berry.
Bolan idolized Eddie Cochran from boyhood.
Bolan was an early Elvis fan, and his rock and roll vocal hiccups come from that era.
Jeepster borrows lines from Howlin' Wolf's You'll Be Mine.
Bolan's early Tyrannosaurus Rex folk records came out of the Dylan-inspired folk scene.

cousins.why: Both are glam, androgynous teen idols with a classic-rock sound.
Both combine sexy boogie grooves with flamboyant style.

artists.name: Queen
artists.summary: Queen combined Brian May's layered guitars, Freddie Mercury's operatic vocals and big harmonies into arena rock. Their 1985 Live Aid set is often called one of the greatest live performances.
know: Brian May built his Red Special guitar with his father.
Bohemian Rhapsody has no repeating chorus.
Every member wrote at least one hit single.

influencedBy.why: Freddie Mercury idolized Hendrix and saw him play many times in London.
Brian May and Mercury named the Beatles as a major influence on their songwriting.
Their early heavy sound follows Led Zeppelin's lead, and Mercury admired Robert Plant.
They named the Who as a model for loud, theatrical rock.
May's early trio Smile followed the Cream model.
Mercury named Aretha Franklin as a favorite singer.
Mercury wrote Crazy Little Thing Called Love as a tribute to Elvis.
John Deacon wrote the Another One Bites the Dust bass line after spending time with Chic's Bernard Edwards.
They wrote and recorded Under Pressure with Bowie.

cousins.why: Both are piano-led, theatrical stadium acts with huge melodies.
Both mix camp, glam and big hooks, and Gaga took her name from Radio Ga Ga.

artists.name: Genesis
artists.summary: Genesis began as a theatrical progressive rock band with Peter Gabriel and became a 1980s pop act with Phil Collins singing. They are one of the best-selling bands of their era.
know: The band formed at Charterhouse, a boarding school in Surrey.
Phil Collins took over as singer after Peter Gabriel left in 1975.
Gabriel performed in elaborate costumes, including a flower mask.
keyAlbums: The Lamb Lies Down on Broadway
songs: I Know What I Like (In Your Wardrobe)

influencedBy.why: Members have said King Crimson's debut showed them what progressive rock could be.
Their early pop songwriting was shaped by the Beatles.
Peter Gabriel named Otis Redding as a key vocal influence after seeing him live.
Gabriel has named Nina Simone among his favorite singers.

cousins.why: Both make theatrical, story-driven art pop with costumes and characters.
Both build long, multi-part concept suites.

artists.name: Yes
artists.summary: Yes made long, complex progressive rock songs built on Jon Anderson's high voice, Steve Howe's guitar and Chris Squire's bass. They returned in the 1980s with the pop hit Owner of a Lonely Heart.
know: Close to the Edge takes up a whole album side with one song.
Roger Dean's fantasy artwork became part of their image.
Owner of a Lonely Heart reached number one in the U.S. in 1984.

influencedBy.why: They covered the Beatles' Every Little Thing on their debut.
They covered the Byrds' I See You on their debut.
They recorded a long version of Simon and Garfunkel's America.
Steve Howe has named jazz guitarists like Wes Montgomery as influences.
Jon Anderson's stacked vocal harmonies draw on folk-rock harmony groups.

cousins.why: Both make dense, cosmic music full of shifting sections.
Both pair virtuoso playing with ambitious, high-concept projects.

artists.name: Rush
artists.summary: Rush were a Canadian trio that combined hard rock power with progressive complexity. Neil Peart's drumming and lyrics made them heroes to musicians.
know: Neil Peart joined in 1974 and wrote most of their lyrics.
2112 includes a side-long suite inspired by Ayn Rand.
They retired after drummer Neil Peart stopped touring in 2015.

influencedBy.why: Geddy Lee has said their debut was heavily influenced by Led Zeppelin.
Alex Lifeson and Lee cited Cream, and they covered Crossroads on Feedback.
Neil Peart named Keith Moon as an early drumming hero, and they covered The Seeker.
Geddy Lee has cited Chris Squire of Yes as a bass influence.
They covered Heart Full of Soul and Shapes of Things on Feedback.
Their move into long progressive suites followed bands like Genesis.
Their early 1980s reggae and new wave touches were inspired by the Police.
Lifeson named Jimi Hendrix as an early guitar influence.

cousins.why: Both make long, technical hard rock with odd meters and big drums.
Both mix heavy riffs with progressive complexity.

artists.name: Fleetwood Mac
artists.summary: Fleetwood Mac began as a British blues band led by Peter Green and became a California soft-rock group with Lindsey Buckingham and Stevie Nicks. Rumours, made as the members' relationships fell apart, is one of the best-selling albums ever.
know: The name combines drummer Mick Fleetwood and bassist John McVie.
Peter Green wrote Black Magic Woman, later a hit for Santana.
Rumours has sold over 40 million copies.

influencedBy.why: Jeremy Spencer's slide playing copied Elmore James, and they covered his songs.
Peter Green named B.B. King as his main influence; King praised Green's tone.
They covered Robert Johnson's Hellhound on My Trail.
Lindsey Buckingham has named Brian Wilson as a major influence on his production.
Stevie Nicks named Janis Joplin as a model for her stage presence.
Nicks has said Grace Slick of Jefferson Airplane was an early inspiration.

cousins.why: Both turn real breakups into confessional, huge-selling songs.
Both are harmony-rich groups with strong female singers.

artists.name: Eagles
artists.summary: The Eagles polished country rock into radio hits, built on clean harmonies and Don Henley and Glenn Frey's songwriting. Their Greatest Hits 1971–1975 is one of the best-selling albums in U.S. history.
know: Several founding members first played as Linda Ronstadt's backing band.
Their Greatest Hits 1971–1975 is one of the best-selling albums in the U.S.
Hotel California won the Grammy for Record of the Year.

influencedBy.why: Their country-rock sound builds directly on the Byrds' Sweetheart of the Rodeo.
They followed Gram Parsons's Flying Burrito Brothers in mixing country and rock in Los Angeles.
Henley and Frey named the Beatles as a songwriting model.
Their close harmonies follow the Everly Brothers' style.
Their stacked harmonies follow the California folk-rock sound of Crosby, Stills and Nash.

cousins.why: Both deliver smooth, polished country-based hits.
Both define the mellow 1970s Southern California sound.

artists.name: Bruce Springsteen
artists.summary: Bruce Springsteen writes cinematic songs about working-class American life, often played with the E Street Band. His marathon live shows are legendary.
know: His nickname is The Boss.
Nebraska was recorded alone on a four-track cassette recorder at home.
He appeared on the covers of Time and Newsweek in the same week in 1975.
keyAlbums: Darkness on the Edge of Town

influencedBy.why: He said seeing Elvis on The Ed Sullivan Show made him want to play guitar.
He said in his Rock Hall speech for Dylan that Like a Rolling Stone 'kicked open the door to your mind.'
Thunder Road names Roy Orbison, and Springsteen inducted Orbison into the Rock Hall.
He covered This Land Is Your Land and cited Guthrie for Nebraska and The Ghost of Tom Joad.
He recorded a whole album of songs Seeger popularized, We Shall Overcome: The Seeger Sessions.
He has said the Animals' We Gotta Get Out of This Place contains every song he ever wrote.
Born to Run's wall of sound copies Phil Spector's productions for the Ronettes.
He backed Chuck Berry as a pickup band member in 1973 and covers his songs often.
He has said Hank Williams's songs shaped the stark writing on Darkness and Nebraska.
He has said the Beatles' arrival made him buy his first guitar.

cousins.why: Both write plain-spoken songs for and about working people.
Both write about small-town restlessness and the urge to escape.

artists.name: Tom Petty and the Heartbreakers
artists.summary: Tom Petty and the Heartbreakers played tight, jangly rock with plainspoken lyrics. Petty also joined Bob Dylan, George Harrison and Roy Orbison in the Traveling Wilburys.
know: Petty met Elvis Presley on a film set in Florida when he was 10.
He fought his record label in 1981 to keep an album's price at $8.98.
He died in 2017 a week after finishing a 40th anniversary tour.
songs: Don't Come Around Here No More

influencedBy.why: Meeting Elvis on a film set as a boy got Petty hooked on rock and roll.
Petty said seeing the Beatles on Ed Sullivan made him decide to start a band.
His jangly 12-string sound comes from the Byrds, and Roger McGuinn covered American Girl.
The Heartbreakers backed Dylan on tour in 1986 and Petty joined him in the Traveling Wilburys.
Petty named the Stones as an early model for a band.
Petty played alongside Orbison in the Traveling Wilburys and called him a hero.

cousins.why: Both play no-frills, twangy rock with classic songwriting.
Both make driving, open-road heartland rock.

artists.name: Aerosmith
artists.summary: Aerosmith, led by Steven Tyler and Joe Perry, became America's top hard rock band of the 1970s and made a big comeback in the late 1980s. Their remake of Walk This Way with Run-DMC helped bring rap to rock radio.
know: They are often called the Bad Boys from Boston.
Dream On was written by Steven Tyler before the band formed.
They retired from touring in 2024 after Tyler injured his voice.
songs: I Don't Want to Miss a Thing

influencedBy.why: Steven Tyler has said Mick Jagger was his main model as a frontman.
They made the Yardbirds' Train Kept A-Rollin' a signature song.
Joe Perry's riff-heavy blues rock follows Jimmy Page's model.
Their glam image and sound share roots with the New York Dolls.
They covered Come Together for the 1978 Sgt. Pepper film.
They covered Peter Green's Stop Messin' Round.

cousins.why: Both are swaggering hard-hitters, and their 1986 Walk This Way remake joined the two styles.
Both are long-lasting 1970s heavy bands with a flamboyant frontman.

artists.name: Kiss
artists.summary: Kiss built a hard rock band around comic-book makeup, fire-breathing and explosive stage shows. Their merchandising and fan army, the Kiss Army, made them a cultural brand.
know: They performed without makeup from 1983 to 1996.
Their 1975 double album Alive! was their commercial breakthrough.
They played their final show at Madison Square Garden in December 2023.
songs: I Was Made for Lovin' You

influencedBy.why: Gene Simmons and Paul Stanley named the Beatles as the band that made them want to play.
Seeing the New York Dolls helped convince them to adopt a glam look and makeup.
Paul Stanley has cited Led Zeppelin as a model for their heavy sound.
Stanley has named Pete Townshend's showmanship as an influence.
Their early riff rock follows the Stones' model.

cousins.why: Both hide behind masks and make the stage show part of the music.
Both built a comic-book universe of costumes and spectacle.
Both kept masked personas that made the band a brand.

artists.name: AC/DC
artists.summary: AC/DC play stripped-down, riff-driven hard rock with Angus Young's schoolboy outfit and energy. Back in Black is one of the best-selling albums in history.
know: Founders Malcolm and Angus Young were born in Scotland.
Singer Bon Scott died in 1980, and Brian Johnson replaced him for Back in Black.
Back in Black has sold an estimated 50 million copies.
keyAlbums: For Those About to Rock We Salute You
songs: You Shook Me All Night Long

influencedBy.why: Angus Young copied Chuck Berry's duckwalk, and they covered School Days.
Angus has named Little Richard among his biggest influences.
Malcolm Young said the early Stones' simple riff rock was a model.
The Young brothers have named Muddy Waters among their blues influences.

cousins.why: Both play loud, simple, unchanging riff music and never chased trends.
Both stuck to one stripped-down formula their whole career.

artists.name: Van Halen
artists.summary: Van Halen, led by guitarist Eddie Van Halen, changed rock guitar with two-handed tapping and a bright, loud sound. David Lee Roth's showmanship made them the biggest party band of the late 1970s and 1980s.
know: Eddie Van Halen built his own Frankenstrat guitar from parts.
Eruption, a solo guitar piece, introduced his tapping style in 1978.
Their contract rider famously banned brown M&M's.

influencedBy.why: Eddie Van Halen said he learned Clapton's solos note for note.
Eddie named Cream's live recordings as the music he learned on.
Their first single was a cover of the Kinks' You Really Got Me.
They covered Oh, Pretty Woman on Diver Down.
Eddie's use of whammy bar and feedback built on Hendrix.
Their early club sets included Led Zeppelin covers.

cousins.why: Both are technical showmen who redefined their instrument for a generation.
Both are led by a guitar hero whose sound defined a style.

artists.name: Steely Dan
artists.summary: Steely Dan, led by Walter Becker and Donald Fagen, made sleek, jazz-chord pop with cryptic, sarcastic lyrics. They used top studio musicians to chase near-perfect records.
know: The band's name comes from William S. Burroughs's novel Naked Lunch.
Becker and Fagen met at Bard College in New York.
Aja won a Grammy for its engineering.

influencedBy.why: They covered Ellington's East St. Louis Toodle-Oo on Pretzel Logic.
Their song Parker's Band on Pretzel Logic is a tribute to Charlie Parker.
Fagen and Becker were jazz fans first, and Miles Davis-era chords run through their writing.
Fagen has named Ray Charles as a key influence on his singing and keyboard style.
Their unusual chord voicings draw on bebop pianists like Monk.

cousins.why: Both put jazz harmony inside smooth, groove-based pop.
Both deliver polished, horn-touched records full of rich chords.

artists.name: Big Star
artists.summary: Big Star, led by Alex Chilton and Chris Bell, made Beatles-inspired power pop that flopped at first but later influenced alternative rock. R.E.M. and the Replacements were among their fans.
know: Alex Chilton had a number one hit as a teenager with the Box Tops' The Letter.
Their label's poor distribution kept their albums out of stores.
The Replacements wrote a song named Alex Chilton.

influencedBy.why: Chilton and Bell built their sound on the Beatles' melodic pop.
Their chiming guitars come straight from the Byrds.
They covered the Kinks' Till the End of the Day.
They covered the Velvet Underground's Femme Fatale on Third.
Their heavier power-pop crunch draws on the Who.

cousins.why: Both wrote fragile, melodic songs that found their audience after the fact.
Both were commercial failures in their time who became cult favorites.

artists.name: Roxy Music
artists.summary: Roxy Music mixed Bryan Ferry's suave crooning with Brian Eno's synthesizer noise and art-school style. They moved from glam to the smooth sound of Avalon.
know: Brian Eno played in the band for its first two albums.
Several members met at art school, and Ferry studied under Richard Hamilton.
Their album covers featured models posed like vintage pin-ups.

influencedBy.why: Ferry and Eno both named the Velvet Underground as a key influence.
Bryan Ferry has said Lead Belly was his first musical hero.
Ferry covered Dylan's A Hard Rain's a-Gonna Fall and later made a whole album of Dylan songs.
Ferry has named Stax soul singers like Otis Redding as early favorites.

cousins.why: Both pair stylish crooning with synthesizers.
Both are suave, tuxedo-ready crooners.

artists.name: Can
artists.summary: Can built long, hypnotic songs from improvised group jams edited on tape. Their locked drum grooves influenced post-punk, electronic music and hip-hop.
know: Two members, Holger Czukay and Irmin Schmidt, studied with composer Karlheinz Stockhausen.
Singer Damo Suzuki was recruited after they saw him busking in Munich.
Their song Spoon was a German hit as a TV crime-show theme.

influencedBy.why: Holger Czukay and Irmin Schmidt named the Velvet Underground as a model for mixing rock with drone.
Czukay said hearing I Am the Walrus convinced him to move into rock.
Jaki Liebezeit's locked repetitive drumming draws on James Brown's funk.
Liebezeit came from free jazz, and the band's long improvisations follow late-1960s Miles Davis.

cousins.why: Both stretch one hypnotic groove over long tracks.
Both build songs on repetitive, motorik grooves.

artists.name: Electric Light Orchestra
artists.summary: Electric Light Orchestra, led by Jeff Lynne, put string sections and big production on Beatles-style pop. They had dozens of hits in the 1970s.
know: ELO grew out of the Move.
Mr. Blue Sky was written during a stay in the Swiss Alps.
Jeff Lynne later produced records for George Harrison, Paul McCartney and Tom Petty.

influencedBy.why: Jeff Lynne said ELO meant to pick up where the Beatles' I Am the Walrus left off.
They had an early hit with Chuck Berry's Roll Over Beethoven.
Lynne idolized Orbison, produced his Mystery Girl and played with him in the Traveling Wilburys.
Their lush, layered vocal harmonies follow Brian Wilson's productions.

cousins.why: Both made lush, studio-perfect 1970s pop.
Both use vocoders and glossy production for feel-good grooves.

artists.name: Eric Clapton
artists.summary: Eric Clapton played in the Yardbirds, John Mayall's Bluesbreakers and Cream before a long solo career. He helped make blues guitar central to rock.
know: Graffiti in 1960s London read 'Clapton is God.'
Layla was written about Pattie Boyd, then married to George Harrison.
He is the only three-time inductee into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame.
keyAlbums: Layla and Other Assorted Love Songs

influencedBy.why: He recorded a full album of Johnson songs, Me and Mr. Johnson, and called him the most important blues musician.
He recorded Riding with the King with B.B. King in 2000.
He named Freddie King as a major early influence and toured with him.
He named Albert King as a key influence on his string bending.
He toured with Muddy Waters in 1979 and called him a father figure.
He has called Buddy Guy the best guitar player alive.
He played on The London Howlin' Wolf Sessions in 1971.
He had a number one hit with Marley's I Shot the Sheriff.
He said Music from Big Pink made him want to leave Cream and play simpler music.
Duane Allman played slide guitar on Layla.
He has said Hendrix changed his sense of what the guitar could do.

cousins.why: Both are blues guitar heroes who brought the blues to rock audiences.
Both are guitar-first blues players with crossover reach.

artists.name: The Police
artists.summary: The Police combined punk energy, reggae rhythms and jazz skill in a trio of Sting, Andy Summers and Stewart Copeland. Synchronicity made them one of the biggest bands in the world in 1983.
know: The band dyed their hair blond for a chewing-gum commercial.
Stewart Copeland's father was a CIA officer.
Every Breath You Take was the biggest U.S. hit of 1983.
songs: Don't Stand So Close to Me

influencedBy.why: Sting has named Bob Marley as the key influence on the band's reggae rhythms.
Sting has called the Beatles his first songwriting model.
Sting played in jazz groups before the Police, and their tight trio playing shows that background.
They started in London's 1977 punk scene with fast, stripped-down songs like Fall Out.

cousins.why: Both mixed punk with Jamaican rhythms in late-1970s Britain.
Both bring off-beat global rhythms into crisp, smart pop rock.

artists.name: Elvis Costello
artists.summary: Elvis Costello came out of the British punk era with clever, angry songs and has since worked in country, soul, jazz and classical. He is one of rock's most versatile songwriters.
know: His real name is Declan MacManus.
He was banned from Saturday Night Live for years after switching songs live in 1977.
He co-wrote songs with Paul McCartney and Burt Bacharach.
songs: (What's So Funny 'Bout) Peace, Love and Understanding

influencedBy.why: He has called the Beatles his first musical love and later wrote with Paul McCartney.
He has named Dylan as a key songwriting influence.
He said Music from Big Pink changed his idea of what a band could be.
He covered Gram Parsons's How Much I've Lied on Almost Blue.
He covered George Jones's A Good Year for the Roses and later sang a duet with Jones.
He covered Hank Williams's Why Don't You Love Me on Almost Blue.
He covered Haggard's Tonight the Bottle Let Me Down on Almost Blue.
Watching the Detectives uses the reggae rhythms he heard in late-1970s London.
His sharp, wordy British pop follows Ray Davies's model.

cousins.why: Both are witty, bitter British songwriters with a literary edge.
Both pack sharp wordplay and humor into tightly built songs.

artists.name: New York Dolls
artists.summary: The New York Dolls mixed trashy rock and roll with glam style and a loose, chaotic energy. They linked early 1970s glam to the New York and London punk scenes.
know: Todd Rundgren produced their 1973 debut album.
Malcolm McLaren briefly managed them before working with the Sex Pistols.
Singer David Johansen later had a hit as his alter ego Buster Poindexter.

influencedBy.why: Johansen and Johnny Thunders modeled their swagger and loose guitar sound on the early Stones.
They covered Pills, a Bo Diddley song, on their debut.
Their look and glam rock crunch drew on Marc Bolan's glam style.
They shared the Stooges' raw, stripped-back attitude and played the same circuits.

cousins.why: A Stones-inspired American band with the same strutting rock and roll feel.
New York rock built on loud guitars and theatrical image.

artists.name: Ramones
artists.summary: The Ramones cut rock and roll down to short, fast songs with buzzsaw guitar and pop melodies. Their first album is often treated as the start of punk rock.
know: Every member adopted the surname Ramone.
Their 1976 debut album ran under 30 minutes.
They played more than 2,000 concerts over 22 years.

influencedBy.why: The band named the Stooges as a major source of their raw, minimal approach.
Seeing the Dolls in New York convinced them a stripped-down band could work.
Their surf themes and harmonies borrow from the Beach Boys, as on Rockaway Beach.
Joey Ramone loved Phil Spector's girl groups, and they covered Baby, I Love You with Spector producing.
Their name comes from Paul McCartney's early alias Paul Ramon, and they cited the Beatles' pop craft.
Their power-chord drive owes much to early Who records.
The simple, distorted riffs of the early Kinks fed into their guitar style.

cousins.why: Fast, loud, stripped-down rock that changed what heavy music could be.
Short, tight rock songs built on a few chords and big hooks.
Stripped hip hop back to hard basics, as the Ramones did with rock.

artists.name: Patti Smith
artists.summary: Patti Smith fused poetry readings with rock and roll, bringing a literary voice to the early New York punk scene. Her album Horses showed punk could be artful and ambitious.
know: John Cale produced her debut album, Horses, in 1975.
Because the Night was co-written with Bruce Springsteen.
She won the National Book Award in 2010 for her memoir Just Kids.

influencedBy.why: Smith has called Dylan a central model for mixing poetry with rock.
Jim Morrison's spoken, poetic performance style shaped her early sets.
She has cited Keith Richards and the Stones as core rock influences.
She has cited Hendrix's improvisational spirit, and Horses was recorded at his Electric Lady Studios.
Her blend of art and street rock follows the Velvet Underground, and John Cale produced Horses.

cousins.why: Spoken-word poetry delivered over music with a political edge.
A female songwriter whose poetic lyrics redefined what her genre could hold.

artists.name: Television
artists.summary: Television brought long, interlocking guitar solos into the CBGB punk scene. Marquee Moon remains a key model for guitar bands that value melody and improvisation.
know: Tom Verlaine and Richard Lloyd traded intricate twin-guitar lines.
They were one of the first bands to play regularly at CBGB.
Richard Hell was an early member before forming the Voidoids.

influencedBy.why: The droning, hypnotic guitar textures recall the Velvets.
Verlaine cited the Byrds' chiming guitars, which echo in their interlocking parts.
Verlaine said free jazz players like Coltrane and Albert Ayler shaped his soloing.
Richard Lloyd has named Keith Richards as a guitar influence.
Their extended guitar improvisation follows the rave-ups of 1960s bands like the Yardbirds.

cousins.why: Long, improvised twin-guitar passages built on interplay.
Players weaving lines around each other rather than strumming chords.

artists.name: Sex Pistols
artists.summary: The Sex Pistols brought punk into British mainstream culture with one album and a handful of singles. Their sound and attitude set off a wave of new bands across the UK.
know: Never Mind the Bollocks was their only studio album.
Their 1976 Manchester gig inspired members of Joy Division, Buzzcocks and the Smiths to start playing.
Guitarist Steve Jones layered many guitar tracks to create the album's thick wall of sound.
keyAlbums: Never Mind the Bollocks, Here's the Sex Pistols

influencedBy.why: They covered No Fun, and Steve Jones built his guitar sound on the Stooges.
Manager Malcolm McLaren had worked with the Dolls, and Jones modeled his playing on Johnny Thunders.
They covered Substitute, and the Who's mod aggression shaped their sound.
Their raw British riffing and London sneer echo the early Kinks.

cousins.why: A group whose blunt, provocative records caused a national uproar.
Raw, loud British rock that bridged punk and metal fans.

artists.name: The Clash
artists.summary: The Clash started as a punk band and grew to take in reggae, dub, rockabilly, funk and early hip hop. London Calling is often named among the greatest rock albums.
know: London Calling was released as a double album priced like a single LP.
They covered Junior Murvin's Police and Thieves on their debut.
Lee Perry produced their single Complete Control.
songs: Should I Stay or Should I Go

influencedBy.why: Joe Strummer said seeing the Pistols made him quit his pub band and join the Clash.
The Ramones' 1976 London shows pushed them toward short, fast songs.
They covered a Perry-produced reggae song and later had Perry produce Complete Control.
Strummer and Mick Jones cited Jamaican reggae, Marley included, as a core influence on their rhythms.
Mick Jones grew up on the Who and their mod power chords.
Jones has named the Stones as his biggest early influence.
Strummer admired Guthrie's protest songs, and his early nickname was Woody.
Their rockabilly side, as on Brand New Cadillac, draws on 1950s rockers like Cochran.

cousins.why: British bands mixing Jamaican music with punk energy and social themes.
Politically charged music that mixed many styles.
Songs of protest and solidarity with a strong groove.

artists.name: Talking Heads
artists.summary: Talking Heads came out of CBGB and moved toward layered funk and African polyrhythms. Their work with Brian Eno widened what a rock band could sound like.
know: Brian Eno produced three of their albums, from More Songs About Buildings and Food to Remain in Light.
Their concert film Stop Making Sense was directed by Jonathan Demme.
David Byrne, Chris Frantz and Tina Weymouth met at the Rhode Island School of Design.

influencedBy.why: Eno produced three albums and co-wrote much of Remain in Light.
Byrne and the band cited Fela's Afrobeat as the model for Remain in Light.
They covered Take Me to the River, written by Al Green and Teenie Hodges.
Their early minimal, art school approach follows the Velvets.
Tina Weymouth and Chris Frantz drew on P-Funk grooves, and Bernie Worrell joined their live band.
Their interlocking funk parts borrow from James Brown's rhythm section.

cousins.why: Long, layered grooves built from interlocking parts.
Art-school musicians who made detached, rhythmic pop.
Tight, guitar-and-bass funk that kept people dancing.

artists.name: Joy Division
artists.summary: Joy Division turned punk's energy into stark, spacious music with melodic bass and cold atmosphere. Their two albums shaped post-punk, goth and much later indie rock.
know: Martin Hannett produced both studio albums for Factory Records.
Peter Hook played melodic lead lines high on the bass.
The remaining members continued as New Order.

influencedBy.why: Members decided to form a band after the Pistols' 1976 Manchester show.
They covered Sister Ray live and cited the Velvets' drone.
Ian Curtis's baritone delivery was often compared to Jim Morrison, whom he admired.
They played Trans-Europe Express before shows and borrowed its mechanical feel.
Curtis was a big Stooges fan, and The Idiot era Iggy shaped their mood.
Bowie's Berlin albums, especially Low, influenced their sound; the band's early name Warsaw came from Bowie's Warszawa.
The repetitive, motorik drumming draws on German bands like Can.

cousins.why: Sparse, haunted music that relies on space and atmosphere.
Dark, brooding songs from the same post-punk era.

artists.name: The Cure
artists.summary: The Cure moved between bleak gothic records and bright pop singles, all led by Robert Smith's voice and guitar. They are one of the most influential bands in goth and alternative rock.
know: Their first single, Killing an Arab, was based on the novel The Stranger.
Robert Smith also played guitar with Siouxsie and the Banshees.
They were inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame in 2019.

influencedBy.why: Robert Smith said playing with the Banshees changed how he approached the band.
Smith has named Bowie a lifelong favorite; Bowie's Low shaped Seventeen Seconds.
Smith has cited Hendrix as his first guitar hero.
Smith has named Nick Drake as a favorite, and his melancholy feel echoes in the band.
Early Cure singles share the sharp, melodic punk-pop of Buzzcocks.
Smith grew up on the Beatles and cites their pop songwriting.

cousins.why: Dark, emotional songs that still became huge pop hits.
Moody, atmospheric music with a strong personal voice.

artists.name: Siouxsie and the Banshees
artists.summary: Siouxsie and the Banshees moved from punk into dark, textured post-punk with inventive guitar and drums. They helped create gothic rock and paved the way for many female-fronted bands.
know: Their first live show was at the 100 Club Punk Festival in 1976.
Robert Smith of the Cure played guitar with them at times.
Their cover of the Beatles' Dear Prudence was a UK top five hit.

influencedBy.why: They covered All Tomorrow's Parties and cited the Velvets' dark tone.
Siouxsie has called Bowie a key early influence on her style and voice.
Glam acts like T. Rex shaped Siouxsie's teenage tastes, and the band covered 20th Century Boy.
The band cited Roxy Music's art rock as a formative influence.
They covered Dear Prudence and Helter Skelter.
They emerged from the Bromley Contingent of Sex Pistols fans.
Their tribal, repetitive drumming draws on German bands such as Can.

cousins.why: A singular British woman with a theatrical, otherworldly sound.
A bold female voice who made strange music popular.

artists.name: Buzzcocks
artists.summary: Manchester punk band that paired buzzsaw guitars with tight, melodic pop songwriting. They wrote the template for pop punk.

Their 1976 EP Spiral Scratch was one of the first self-released punk records in Britain.
Singles Going Steady collected their run of late-70s singles and became a pop-punk touchstone.
keyAlbums: Another Music in a Different Kitchen
songs: Ever Fallen in Love (With Someone You Shouldn't've)

influencedBy.why: Shelley and Devoto started the band after driving to London to see the Sex Pistols, then booked them in Manchester.
Shelley cited the Velvet Underground's drone and economy as a model for their guitar sound.
Raw, simple Stooges riffs were part of the band's early covers and attack.
Their short, hook-first songs draw on 60s Beatles pop craft.
Shelley named Can's repetitive grooves as an influence on his guitar playing.

cousins.why: Power pop with crunch, built on short, perfect hooks.
Relentless melodic hooks, just played much faster.

artists.name: Blondie
artists.summary: Blondie came out of the CBGB punk scene but wrote tight, hook-driven pop songs and moved freely into disco, reggae and rap. They showed that a New York punk band could top the pop charts without losing its edge.

Call Me was written and produced with Giorgio Moroder for the film American Gigolo.
Rapture became the first US number one single to feature rapping.

influencedBy.why: Their melodic hooks and Debbie Harry's vocal style borrow openly from 1960s girl-group pop.
The Dolls showed the downtown New York scene that trashy, catchy rock and roll could be a style of its own.

Working with Moroder on Call Me brought his driving synth disco production directly into their sound.
The steady four-on-the-floor disco of Heart of Glass follows the template of Summer's electronic dance hits.
Rapture was their tribute to the Bronx rap scene and names Grandmaster Flash directly.

cousins.why: A downtown New York singer who blended dance music and pop into hit records.
Sleek, guitar-led disco built on crisp hooks and a strong groove.

artists.name: Devo
artists.summary: Devo played jerky, mechanical rock built on stiff rhythms, angular guitar and early synthesizers, wrapped in a strong visual concept. Their robotic approach helped define American new wave and early synth-pop.
know: Their debut album was produced by Brian Eno in Germany.
Their stiff, rebuilt cover of the Rolling Stones' Satisfaction was an early calling card.
Whip It reached the US top 20 in 1980, and Mark Mothersbaugh later became a prolific film and TV composer.

influencedBy.why: Kraftwerk's machine-like precision and synthesizer textures fed directly into Devo's robotic arrangements.
Beefheart's lopsided rhythms and odd, angular guitar figures are a clear model for Devo's twitchy song structures.
Eno produced their debut and pushed its electronic treatments and studio experimentation.

cousins.why: A concept-driven band pairing synthesizers with tight, mechanical pop.
Satirical, highly controlled rock with a strong conceptual framework.

artists.name: Judas Priest
artists.summary: Judas Priest stripped the blues out of heavy rock and replaced it with twin lead guitars, fast riffs and Rob Halford's high operatic voice, defining the classic heavy metal sound of the late 1970s and 1980s.
know: The twin lead guitar partnership of K.K. Downing and Glenn Tipton became a model for later metal bands.
Painkiller (1990) introduced drummer Scott Travis and his fast double-bass playing.
They were inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame in 2022.

influencedBy.why: K.K. Downing has named Hendrix as the guitarist who made him pick up the instrument, and his expressive lead style shaped Downing's solos.
Fellow Birmingham band whose heavy riffing showed Priest the path away from standard blues rock.
Cream's extended, loud blues rock jams were part of the early band's musical starting point.
Zeppelin's dynamic hard rock and high vocal range were a widely noted reference for early Priest.
Deep Purple's fast, classically tinged hard rock riffs and screaming vocals foreshadow Priest's approach.

cousins.why: Operatic, theatrical lead vocals carrying hard-hitting guitar rock.
Riff-first, no-frills hard rock that set a standard for its genre.

artists.name: Motörhead

Phil Taylor's double-bass drumming on Overkill is widely cited as a starting point for thrash drumming.
songs: The Chase Is Better Than the Catch

influencedBy.why: Lemmy called Little Richard a primary inspiration, and Motörhead's pounding piano-style rock and roll drive comes straight from him.
Berry's fast, chugging rock and roll guitar patterns sit underneath many Motörhead riffs.
Lemmy saw the Beatles at the Cavern Club and said they shaped his idea of what a band could be.

Cochran's raw, fast rockabilly was among the 1950s records Lemmy named as formative.

cousins.why: Fast, loud, minimal songs that cut rock back to its basics.
Relentless speed and volume that bridged punk and metal audiences.

artists.name: Elton John
artists.summary: Elton John and lyricist Bernie Taupin wrote one of the longest runs of hit singles of the 1970s. He paired piano-driven rock with flamboyant showmanship.
know: He was born Reginald Dwight and studied at the Royal Academy of Music as a teenager.
He met Bernie Taupin in 1967 after both answered the same Liberty Records advert.
'Candle in the Wind 1997' became one of the best-selling singles ever.

influencedBy.why: Elton has said seeing Little Richard pound the piano made him want to be a rock and roll pianist.
His standing-at-the-piano, kick-the-stool stage act draws directly on Lewis.
Elton and Taupin have said Music from Big Pink shaped the Americana songs of Tumbleweed Connection.
Elton has cited Ray Charles's gospel-rooted piano and voice as an early model.
Presley's records were among the first rock and roll he heard as a child in the 1950s.
He recorded 'Lucy in the Sky with Diamonds' with John Lennon and drew on their melodic songwriting.

cousins.why: Theatrical, piano-led British rock with a showman at the front.
A fellow 1970s glam star who used costume and persona as part of the act.

artists.name: Billy Joel
artists.summary: Billy Joel is a piano-playing songwriter whose character-driven songs about New York and Long Island life made him one of the best-selling solo artists in the U.S.
know: 'Piano Man' was based on his time playing at a Los Angeles piano bar.
He boxed as a teenager and broke his nose in the ring.
He played a monthly residency at Madison Square Garden from 2014 to 2024.

influencedBy.why: Joel has said seeing the Beatles on The Ed Sullivan Show made him decide to be a musician.
He named his daughter Alexa Ray after Ray Charles and has called him a major influence.
'Say Goodbye to Hollywood' was written as an homage to Ronnie Spector and the 'Be My Baby' sound, and she later recorded it.

cousins.why: East Coast storyteller writing about working people and their towns.
Fellow 1970s singer-songwriter with a long run of radio staples.

artists.name: Carole King
artists.summary: Carole King wrote dozens of 1960s hits with Gerry Goffin before her album Tapestry made her the defining singer-songwriter of the early 1970s.

She has been inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame twice, as a songwriter and as a performer.
songs: (You Make Me Feel Like) A Natural Woman

cousins.why: The other defining woman singer-songwriter of the early 1970s Laurel Canyon scene.
Wrote hits for other singers before becoming a star with his own records.

artists.name: ABBA
artists.summary: The Swedish quartet won Eurovision in 1974 with 'Waterloo' and became one of the best-selling acts in pop history. Benny Andersson and Björn Ulvaeus wrote precise, often melancholy songs that still fill dance floors.
know: The name is an acronym of the members' first names: Agnetha, Björn, Benny and Anni-Frid.
The stage musical Mamma Mia! is built entirely from their songs.
Their 2021 album Voyage came 40 years after their previous one.

influencedBy.why: Björn and Benny have said the Beatles were their biggest songwriting influence.
Benny has cited Brian Wilson's harmonies and arrangements as a model.
Their early records used Phil Spector-style layered production associated with the Ronettes.

cousins.why: A 1970s hit machine also made up of two couples whose breakups fed the songs.
Lush, meticulously produced 1970s pop with big hooks.

artists.name: Bee Gees
artists.summary: Brothers Barry, Robin and Maurice Gibb had hits across five decades, from 1960s baroque ballads to the falsetto disco of the Saturday Night Fever soundtrack.
know: The Saturday Night Fever soundtrack (1977) became one of the best-selling albums of all time.
Producer Arif Mardin encouraged Barry Gibb to try the falsetto that became their disco signature.
They wrote 'Islands in the Stream' for Kenny Rogers and Dolly Parton.

The Gibbs cited the Everlys as the model for their sibling harmony.
Barry Gibb wrote 'To Love Somebody' with Otis Redding in mind, reflecting their love of Southern soul.

cousins.why: Another architect of the late-1970s disco sound.
Disco hitmakers who were also first-rate songwriters and players.

artists.name: Kate Bush
artists.summary: Kate Bush is an English art-pop singer, writer and producer whose theatrical, literary songs made her one of the most singular voices in British music.

David Gilmour of Pink Floyd paid for her early demo recordings.
'Running Up That Hill' returned to the charts in 2022 after it was used in Stranger Things.

Bush has named Elton as an early hero and recorded a cover of 'Rocket Man' in 1991.
She has cited Bowie as a major influence on her theatrical approach to pop.
She has named Roxy Music among the bands she loved as a teenager.
Their studio experimentation is a clear model for her self-produced albums.

cousins.why: An idiosyncratic singer-producer building whole sonic worlds around her voice.
A fiercely independent writer who kept stretching what a pop song could be.
An English artist whose albums are full of characters, myth and theatre.

artists.name: Al Green
artists.summary: Al Green's soft falsetto over Willie Mitchell's Hi Records productions produced some of the most sensual soul of the 1970s, before he became a pastor and gospel singer.

I'm Still in Love with You

His breakout album opens with a credited slow remake of their 'I Can't Get Next to You'.
He recorded a credited cover of 'How Can You Mend a Broken Heart'.
He recorded a credited cover of Williams's 'I'm So Lonesome I Could Cry'.

artists.name: Isaac Hayes

He voiced Chef on South Park.

artists.name: Bill Withers

cousins.why: A plainspoken storyteller who started writing while working a regular job.
Spare, direct songs with a warm voice and acoustic guitar.

artists.name: Parliament-Funkadelic
artists.summary: George Clinton's twin bands Parliament and Funkadelic built a sci-fi funk universe that, through samples, became the backbone of West Coast hip-hop.

Dr. Dre's G-funk sound drew heavily on P-Funk samples.

cousins.why: A sprawling, satirical bandleader with a huge cast of virtuoso players.
Southern hip-hop that carried P-Funk's cosmic weirdness forward.

artists.name: Earth, Wind & Fire
