cousins.why: A band blending Latin rhythms, rock and spiritual themes.
A horn-heavy groove band mixing jazz, funk and African rhythms.
Jazz-fusion with big grooves and global influences.

artists.name: Chic
artists.summary: Chic, led by guitarist Nile Rodgers and bassist Bernard Edwards, made disco's most elegant records and later produced hits for Diana Ross, David Bowie and Madonna.
know: 'Le Freak' was written after they were turned away at the door of Studio 54.
The 'Good Times' bass line was used in the Sugarhill Gang's 'Rapper's Delight'.
Nile Rodgers co-wrote and played on Daft Punk's 'Get Lucky'.

influencedBy.why: Nile Rodgers has said Roxy Music's stylish image and sound inspired Chic's concept.
Rodgers's chopped rhythm guitar comes out of James Brown's funk.

cousins.why: Disco-loving dance music that later recruited Rodgers himself.
New York band that fused art rock with tight funk grooves.

artists.name: Donna Summer
artists.summary: Donna Summer was the defining voice of disco, and her work with Giorgio Moroder, especially the all-synthesizer 'I Feel Love', laid groundwork for electronic dance music.
know: She performed in a German production of Hair in the late 1960s.
Brian Eno told David Bowie that 'I Feel Love' would change the sound of club music.
Bad Girls (1979) was a No. 1 double album.

influencedBy.why: Moroder produced and co-wrote her biggest records, shaping her synth-driven sound.
Summer said hearing Mahalia Jackson as a child made her want to sing.

cousins.why: The electronic pioneers whose machine sound fed into 'I Feel Love'.
The house DJ who carried disco into electronic dance music.

artists.name: Gil Scott-Heron
artists.summary: Gil Scott-Heron was a poet and musician whose politically charged spoken-word pieces, often with keyboardist Brian Jackson, are seen as a forerunner of hip-hop.
know: He published a novel, The Vulture, in 1970.
'The Revolution Will Not Be Televised' first appeared on Small Talk at 125th and Lenox (1970).
His final album, I'm New Here (2010), was remixed by Jamie xx.
songs: The Revolution Will Not Be Televised
Home Is Where the Hatred Is

influencedBy.why: He wrote 'Lady Day and John Coltrane' about how Coltrane's music sustained him.
'Lady Day and John Coltrane' names Holiday as a source of strength and inspiration.

cousins.why: Political hip-hop that carried his message forward.
A poet-songwriter whose words made him the voice of a movement.

artists.name: DJ Kool Herc
artists.summary: Jamaican-born DJ whose Bronx block parties are widely treated as the starting point of hip hop. He invented the idea of extending a record's drum break so dancers could keep going.
know: Born Clive Campbell in Kingston, Jamaica, he moved to the Bronx as a boy in 1967.
His August 11, 1973 party at 1520 Sedgwick Avenue is often cited as hip hop's birthday.
He looped breaks with two copies of the same record, a technique he called the Merry-Go-Round.
songs: Apache (Incredible Bongo Band, a Herc staple)
Give It Up or Turnit a Loose (James Brown, a Herc staple)
Bongo Rock (Incredible Bongo Band, a Herc staple)

influencedBy.why: James Brown breaks were the core of Herc's sets, and he switched to funk records when reggae did not move Bronx crowds.
Herc carried over the Jamaican sound system culture of big custom speakers and talking over instrumentals that Tubby's world defined.

cousins.why: Another DJ who built a whole genre out of what he played at parties.
A sound system figure whose technical tricks became the foundation of a new genre.

artists.name: Grandmaster Flash and the Furious Five
artists.summary: Bronx DJ and his crew of rappers who turned DJing into a precise craft and then made 'The Message,' the record that showed rap could report on real life.
know: In 2007 they became the first hip hop act inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame.
Flash refined cutting and backspinning, cueing breaks with headphones so the mix never dropped.
'The Adventures of Grandmaster Flash on the Wheels of Steel' (1981) was built live from records by Chic, Queen and Blondie.
songs: The Adventures of Grandmaster Flash on the Wheels of Steel

influencedBy.why: Flash took Herc's break-looping idea and made it tight and precise on the turntables.
James Brown breaks were basic material for Flash's sets and early mixes.
Chic's 'Good Times' is a central piece of 'Wheels of Steel.'
'Another One Bites the Dust' is cut into 'Wheels of Steel.'

cousins.why: Turned grim city life into sharp spoken social commentary.
A band that wrote about urban decay and shared stages with Flash in 1981.

artists.name: The Sugarhill Gang
artists.summary: A trio put together by Sugar Hill Records whose 'Rapper's Delight' was the first rap record most of the world ever heard.
know: 'Rapper's Delight' (1979) was the first rap single to reach the US Top 40.
Sylvia Robinson of Sugar Hill Records assembled the group.
The track's groove replays the bassline of Chic's 'Good Times.'

influencedBy.why: 'Rapper's Delight' is built on a replayed version of Chic's 'Good Times' groove.
Their party-rap style came from the Bronx park-jam scene that Herc started.

cousins.why: A producer-assembled act that became the first big hit for a new sound.
Turned a club sound into a worldwide radio hit in the same disco era.

artists.name: Kraftwerk
artists.summary: German group that built pop music almost entirely from synthesizers and drum machines. They are the starting point for synth-pop, electro, techno and much of hip-hop.
know: Ralf Hütter and Florian Schneider founded the group and built their own Kling Klang studio.
Afrika Bambaataa's "Planet Rock" (1982) borrowed from "Trans-Europe Express" and "Numbers."
They were inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame in 2021.

influencedBy.why: Their minimal, repetitive drone shared ground with the Velvets, a band admired in their Düsseldorf circle.
Can's motorik repetition was part of the same German scene Kraftwerk came out of.
"Autobahn" is often heard as a sly nod to the Beach Boys' car songs.

cousins.why: Robot personas and machine-age concepts.
Art-school minds remaking pop with rhythm.

artists.name: Giorgio Moroder
artists.summary: Italian producer who fused disco with synthesizers. His work with Donna Summer laid the groundwork for electronic dance music.
know: He produced Donna Summer's "I Feel Love" (1977), built around a Moog synthesizer sequence.
He won Oscars for the Midnight Express score and the songs "Flashdance... What a Feeling" and "Take My Breath Away."
He tells his own story on Daft Punk's "Giorgio by Moroder" (2013).

influencedBy.why: His sequenced synthesizer disco followed Kraftwerk's lead in making pop with machines.

cousins.why: Studio architects of disco's sound.
A producer whose sound defined other people's hits.

artists.name: Brian Eno
artists.summary: English musician and producer who coined ambient music and treated the studio as an instrument. He has shaped records by Bowie, Talking Heads, U2 and Coldplay.
know: He was a founding member of Roxy Music.
His 1978 album Ambient 1: Music for Airports gave ambient music its name.
He created the Oblique Strategies cards with painter Peter Schmidt.
keyAlbums: My Life in the Bush of Ghosts

influencedBy.why: Eno famously said the Velvets' first album sold few copies but everyone who bought one started a band.
Eno championed Fela's Afrobeat and its interlocking grooves shaped his work with Talking Heads.

cousins.why: Used the studio to build mood and space.
Long-form, atmospheric sound design.

artists.name: Yellow Magic Orchestra
artists.summary: Japanese trio of Haruomi Hosono, Ryuichi Sakamoto and Yukihiro Takahashi. They were electronic pop pioneers whose records influenced techno and hip-hop.
know: "Firecracker" is a cover of an exotica tune by Martin Denny.
Their 1981 album BGM was one of the first to use the Roland TR-808 drum machine.
"Behind the Mask" was later recorded by Michael Jackson and Eric Clapton.

influencedBy.why: YMO followed Kraftwerk in building pop songs from synthesizers and sequencers.
Moroder's sequenced synth disco shaped their dance-floor side.

cousins.why: Witty, conceptual new wave built on machines.
Electronic pop with dance-floor impact.

artists.name: Bob Marley and the Wailers
artists.summary: Jamaican group led by Bob Marley, with Peter Tosh and Bunny Wailer in the early years. They took roots reggae and Rastafarian themes to a worldwide audience.
know: Eric Clapton's 1974 cover of "I Shot the Sheriff" went to number one in the US.
Marley survived a shooting in 1976, two days before the Smile Jamaica concert.
The 1984 compilation Legend is one of the best-selling albums of all time.

influencedBy.why: "One Love" credits and quotes Curtis Mayfield's "People Get Ready," and the early Wailers modeled their harmonies on the Impressions.
Perry produced the Wailers' Soul Rebels and Soul Revolution sessions and sharpened their sound.
New Orleans R&B like Fats Domino's, heard on Jamaican radio, fed the ska the Wailers started in.

cousins.why: A protest songwriter who became a global symbol.
Soul music carrying a spiritual and political message.

artists.name: Lee "Scratch" Perry
artists.summary: Jamaican producer whose Black Ark studio turned out some of reggae's strangest and most influential records. He was a dub pioneer and an early producer of Bob Marley.
know: He built the Black Ark studio in his Kingston backyard in 1973.
He produced the Clash's "Complete Control" (1977).
He produced Junior Murvin's "Police and Thieves" and Max Romeo's "Chase the Devil."
keyAlbums: Roast Fish Collie Weed & Corn Bread

influencedBy.why: He shared King Tubby's approach of stripping and echoing tracks into dub versions.

cousins.why: A cosmic eccentric with his own mythology.
A producer whose feel and textures were his signature.

artists.name: King Tubby
artists.summary: Jamaican sound engineer who invented dub by remixing reggae tracks on a mixing desk. His use of echo, reverb and dropouts became the basis of remix culture.
know: He was an electronics repairman who ran the Home Town Hi-Fi sound system.
He built his own effects and mixed dub versions live at his small studio.
He was shot and killed outside his home in 1989.

influencedBy.why: He traded tapes and ideas with Perry as the two developed dub together.

cousins.why: A Jamaican sound-system man who built a new genre at the turntables.
A producer-engineer known for his unique treatment of sound.

artists.name: Jimmy Cliff
artists.summary: Jamaican singer and actor who helped introduce reggae to the world. His starring role in The Harder They Come and its soundtrack were a breakthrough for the genre.
know: He starred as Ivanhoe Martin in the 1972 film The Harder They Come.
He was inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame in 2010.
Bob Dylan called his song "Vietnam" the best protest song he had heard.
songs: You Can Get It If You Really Want

influencedBy.why: Like other early ska singers, he drew on the New Orleans R&B of Fats Domino heard on Jamaican radio.

cousins.why: A soulful, gospel-touched voice with crossover appeal.
Soul ballads delivered with deep feeling.

artists.name: The Specials
artists.summary: Multiracial English band that revived ska with punk energy. Through their 2 Tone label they led a movement against racism in late-1970s Britain.
know: Keyboardist Jerry Dammers founded the 2 Tone record label.
Elvis Costello produced their 1979 debut album.
"Ghost Town" hit number one in the UK during the 1981 riots.

influencedBy.why: They took the 1960s Jamaican ska and rocksteady of acts like Toots and the Maytals and sped it up.
They toured with the Clash in 1978 and shared their punk politics.
Punk's attitude and speed gave their ska its urgency.

cousins.why: Sharp, socially aware British guitar pop.
A band that mixed punk and Jamaican music.

artists.name: Fela Kuti
artists.summary: Nigerian bandleader who created Afrobeat from highlife, jazz and funk. His long, political songs attacked military rule and made him a hero across Africa.
know: He declared his Lagos compound, the Kalakuta Republic, independent from Nigeria.
Soldiers raided Kalakuta in 1977, and his mother died from injuries in the attack.
Drummer Tony Allen was his key partner in building the Afrobeat sound.

influencedBy.why: After a 1969 stay in the US, Fela folded James Brown's funk into his highlife-jazz band to make Afrobeat.

cousins.why: Long funk grooves led by a larger-than-life figure.
Music used as a political weapon.

artists.name: Stevie Ray Vaughan
artists.summary: The fiery Texas guitarist who led a 1980s blues revival with his band Double Trouble. His heavy tone and speed made blues guitar a mainstream force again.
know: He played lead guitar on David Bowie's Let's Dance in 1983.
His debut album Texas Flood came out the same year.
He died in a helicopter crash after a show in Wisconsin in 1990.

influencedBy.why: Studied Albert's bends closely and later jammed with him on TV.
Covered Voodoo Child and Little Wing and openly idolized Hendrix.
Named Freddie King as a key early guitar hero.
Cited Buddy Guy's attack and tone as a major inspiration.
Drew on the Texas electric tradition T-Bone started.

cousins.why: Blues-based guitar hero with mass appeal.
1980s guitar virtuoso who redefined the instrument's role.

artists.name: George Strait
artists.summary: The King of Country, who kept traditional fiddle and steel sounds on the radio through the 1980s and 90s and scored about 60 number-one hits.
know: He has more number-one singles than any other country artist.
His backing band is the Ace in the Hole Band.
Ocean Front Property (1987) was the first album to debut at number one on the country chart.
songs: All My Ex's Live in Texas

influencedBy.why: He has named Haggard as one of his main influences.
His Ace in the Hole Band plays a lot of western swing in the Wills tradition.
He has cited Jones as one of the singers he grew up on.
His smooth phrasing follows the Frizzell style.

cousins.why: A steady, classy performer with decades of hits.
An effortless interpreter of songs with a long run of hits.

artists.name: Dwight Yoakam
artists.summary: Singer who revived the Bakersfield sound in the 1980s, building a following in Los Angeles rock clubs after Nashville turned him down.
know: He built his early following playing LA punk and roots clubs alongside bands like X.
He brought Buck Owens out of retirement for their 1988 number one "Streets of Bakersfield."
He is also an actor, notably in Sling Blade.
keyAlbums: Buenas Noches from a Lonely Room

influencedBy.why: Owens was his hero, and he coaxed him back to record "Streets of Bakersfield" together.
Haggard's Bakersfield records are the core of his sound.
He covered "Suspicious Minds" in 1992.

cousins.why: Revived a raw roots sound for a younger crowd.
Brought a classic retro sound back during a slick era.

artists.name: Tracy Chapman
artists.summary: Singer-songwriter whose spare debut album, with "Fast Car", brought socially aware folk back to the pop charts in 1988.
know: Her breakthrough came at the 1988 Nelson Mandela 70th Birthday Tribute concert at Wembley.
She studied at Tufts University.
In 2023 she became the first Black songwriter to win CMA Song of the Year, for Luke Combs' cover of "Fast Car."

influencedBy.why: Her acoustic protest songs follow the folk revival path Baez set.
She continues the line of Black women folk singers that Odetta started.

cousins.why: A thoughtful, socially aware voice.
Music as a vehicle for social justice.

artists.name: U2
artists.summary: U2 grew from Dublin post-punk into one of the biggest bands in the world, known for The Edge's echoing guitar and Bono's soaring vocals and activism. The Joshua Tree and Achtung Baby are their landmarks.
know: The four members formed the band at Mount Temple school in 1976.
They have won 22 Grammy Awards.
The Edge built his sound around delay effects.
songs: I Still Haven't Found What I'm Looking For

influencedBy.why: Bono has said the Ramones made them believe they could be a band.
The Edge said seeing the Clash in 1977 changed everything for them.
Bono and the Edge named Patti Smith's Horses as a key influence.
The Edge named Tom Verlaine of Television as an influence on his guitar.
Joy Division's producer Martin Hannett produced their early single 11 O'Clock Tick Tock, and they cited Joy Division.
Bono met Dylan in 1984, and Dylan co-wrote and sang on Love Rescue Me.
They recorded When Love Comes to Town with B.B. King.
Johnny Cash sang lead on The Wanderer on Zooropa.
Bono and the Edge wrote She's a Mystery to Me for Roy Orbison.
Brian Eno co-produced The Unforgettable Fire, The Joshua Tree and Achtung Baby.
They recorded Achtung Baby at Hansa Studios in Berlin, inspired by Bowie's work there.
Bono has named John Lennon as a key influence.

cousins.why: Both make huge, earnest anthems with a spiritual edge.
Both pair political and spiritual themes with stadium-size ambition.

artists.name: Guns N' Roses
artists.summary: Guns N' Roses brought a raw, dangerous edge back to hard rock in the late 1980s. Appetite for Destruction is the best-selling debut album in U.S. history.
know: Appetite for Destruction has sold over 30 million copies.
Slash's guitar intro to Sweet Child o' Mine started as a warm-up exercise.
Axl Rose and Slash reunited for the Not in This Lifetime tour in 2016.

influencedBy.why: Slash has said Aerosmith's Rocks made him want to play guitar.
Their bluesy, swaggering sound follows the Stones' model.
Slash named Jimmy Page as an early guitar influence.
They covered the New York Dolls' Human Being on The Spaghetti Incident?
They covered the Sex Pistols' Black Leather on The Spaghetti Incident?
Axl Rose named Elton John as an influence on November Rain and performed with him in 1992.
Axl Rose has called Freddie Mercury a hero and played the Freddie Mercury Tribute Concert.
They had a hit with Dylan's Knockin' on Heaven's Door.
Their hard-driving riffs draw on AC/DC, and Axl Rose later sang for AC/DC on tour.

cousins.why: Both had a dangerous, banned-from-the-radio Los Angeles image.
Both were the defining heavy bands of the late 1980s.

artists.name: New Order
artists.summary: New Order fused post-punk guitar and bass with drum machines, sequencers and New York club music. They became the main bridge between indie rock and electronic dance music in the 1980s.
know: They were formed by the remaining members of Joy Division in 1980.
Blue Monday (1983) is often cited as the best-selling 12-inch single ever released.
Peter Hook's melodic high-register bass lines act as a lead instrument in many of their songs.

influencedBy.why: New Order grew directly out of Joy Division, carrying over its melodic bass lines and stark atmosphere.
The band has named Kraftwerk as the key model for building songs around sequencers and drum machines.
Bernard Sumner has credited Moroder's sequenced disco productions as an inspiration for their electronic turn.
The band has said Blue Monday borrowed ideas from a Donna Summer track produced by Moroder.
The house rhythms of Technique reflect the Chicago club sound that Knuckles helped create.

cousins.why: A British band that turned synthesizers and drum machines into dark, melodic pop.
A rock-minded act built around dance grooves and analog synths.

artists.name: The Smiths
artists.summary: The Smiths paired Johnny Marr's intricate, chiming guitar arrangements with Morrissey's distinctive crooning vocals. They became the defining British indie band of the 1980s and shaped guitar pop for decades.
know: They released all four studio albums on the independent label Rough Trade.
Meat Is Murder (1985) reached number one on the UK album chart.
Johnny Marr often layered several guitar parts to create a full, ringing sound without keyboards.
songs: There Is a Light That Never Goes Out

influencedBy.why: Morrissey ran the UK fan club for the New York Dolls and has called them his first musical love.
Marr's ringing, arpeggiated guitar draws on the jangle sound Roger McGuinn developed.
Marr has praised Nile Rodgers, and his rhythmic, chord-based guitar parts show that funk influence.
Marr has cited Phil Spector's girl-group productions as a model for the layered sound he wanted.

cousins.why: A guitar-pop band with chiming arrangements and a devoted following.
Melancholy, literate songs carried by intricate acoustic guitar.

artists.name: R.E.M.
artists.summary: R.E.M. combined Peter Buck's chiming arpeggiated guitar with murmured, melodic vocals and folk-rock textures. They grew from college radio favorites into a major band and opened the mainstream to American alternative rock.
know: Their debut album Murmur was named Rolling Stone's album of the year for 1983.
Out of Time (1991) built its biggest hit around a mandolin riff.
They were inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame in 2007.

influencedBy.why: Michael Stipe has said hearing Patti Smith's Horses made him want to make music.
They covered several Velvet Underground songs and shared their droning, understated guitar approach.
Buck's ringing Rickenbacker arpeggios echo the jangle guitar sound of the Byrds.
Television's interlocking, clean guitar lines shaped the spare post-punk side of their early records.
Big Star's melodic guitar pop was a touchstone for their circle of Southern college rock bands.

cousins.why: Jangling, Byrds-influenced guitar rock with strong melodies.
Rootsy, atmospheric American songs built on ensemble playing.

artists.name: Black Flag
artists.summary: Black Flag played fast, abrasive hardcore driven by Greg Ginn's atonal guitar and later slowed it into heavy, sludgy forms. Through constant touring and their label SST, they built the independent network American underground rock relied on.
know: Guitarist Greg Ginn founded SST Records, which also released Hüsker Dü and Sonic Youth.
Henry Rollins joined as their fourth vocalist in 1981, just before Damaged.
The slow, heavy second side of My War is often cited as a forerunner of sludge metal and grunge.

influencedBy.why: Ginn has cited Black Sabbath, and their slow, crushing riffs shaped the heavy songs on My War.
The Stooges' raw, repetitive riffing laid groundwork for their blunt, aggressive sound.
The Ramones' short, fast songs were the starting point for the speed of early hardcore.
Ginn was a devoted Grateful Dead fan, and their long improvised jams fed his free-form soloing.

cousins.why: Loud, fast and relentless music that bridged punk and metal.
Extreme speed and aggression with chaotic, atonal guitar solos.

artists.name: Minor Threat
artists.summary: Minor Threat played extremely fast, tightly drilled hardcore songs, most under two minutes. Their records and their do-it-yourself label set the template for the Washington and wider American hardcore scenes.
know: Ian MacKaye and Jeff Nelson co-founded Dischord Records to release their music.
Their complete recorded output fits on a single compilation, Complete Discography.
Ian MacKaye later co-founded the influential post-hardcore band Fugazi.

influencedBy.why: MacKaye has repeatedly credited Bad Brains' speed and precision as the model for his band.
The Ramones' stripped-down, fast songwriting was a foundation for their compact songs.
Black Flag's early records showed DC bands how fast and abrasive American hardcore could be.

cousins.why: Short, fast, tightly played songs pushed to extremes of speed.
Dense, urgent music that conveyed intensity through tight arrangement.

artists.name: Bad Brains
artists.summary: Bad Brains played hardcore at blinding speed with the precision of trained musicians and alternated it with deep roots reggae. They helped invent hardcore punk and proved it could carry real virtuosity.
know: They started as a jazz fusion band called Mind Power before turning to punk.
Rock for Light (1983) was produced by Ric Ocasek of the Cars.
Their albums often switch between full-speed hardcore and slow reggae tracks.

influencedBy.why: Bob Marley's music drew them to reggae, which became half of their sound.
Hearing the Ramones helped convert the band from fusion to fast punk.
The Sex Pistols' aggression was part of what pulled them into punk rock.

cousins.why: Virtuosic players merging heavy guitar with another genre's groove.
A band that fused punk energy with Jamaican rhythms.

artists.name: Hüsker Dü
artists.summary: Hüsker Dü played hardcore at full speed but buried strong pop melodies under walls of distorted guitar. They pointed the way from hardcore to melodic alternative rock and later grunge.
know: Zen Arcade (1984) was an ambitious double album recorded in a matter of days for SST.
They were among the first American hardcore bands to sign to a major label, joining Warner Bros. in 1986.
Bob Mould and Grant Hart split the songwriting and lead vocals.
songs: Don't Want to Know If You Are Lonely

influencedBy.why: Bob Mould has said the Ramones' first album changed his life and showed him how to play.
They released a roaring cover of the Byrds' Eight Miles High, showing their love of 1960s melody.
Grant Hart's pop songwriting draws on Beatles-style melody and harmony.
Their early speed and noise came out of the hardcore circuit Black Flag built, including SST.

cousins.why: Loud, powerful guitar rock built on strong pop melodies.
Melodic guitar songs with a raw edge and a cult following.

artists.name: The Replacements
artists.summary: The Replacements moved from ragged punk to heartfelt guitar rock, led by Paul Westerberg's melodic, conversational songwriting. Their loose, emotional records became a model for American indie and alternative rock.
know: They debuted on the Minneapolis independent label Twin/Tone.
Tim (1985) was produced by Tommy Ramone.
Their song Alex Chilton honors the Big Star singer, who played on Pleased to Meet Me.

influencedBy.why: Westerberg wrote a song named after Alex Chilton and drew on Big Star's bittersweet power pop.
The Dolls' sloppy, swaggering rock and roll is a clear model for their loose sound.
Their ragged, riff-based rock and roll owes a lot to the Stones' looser side.

cousins.why: Heartfelt, melodic guitar rock with plain-spoken songwriting.
Sharp, emotional songwriting delivered with punk-era energy.

artists.name: Sonic Youth
artists.summary: Sonic Youth rebuilt the electric guitar with alternate tunings, prepared instruments and waves of feedback, then shaped that noise into songs. They became elder statesmen of the American underground and opened doors for 1990s alternative rock.
know: They used dozens of unusual guitar tunings and sometimes wedged objects under the strings.
Thurston Moore and Lee Ranaldo both played in Glenn Branca's guitar ensembles before the band took off.
Daydream Nation (1988) was added to the Library of Congress National Recording Registry.

influencedBy.why: The Velvets' drones, feedback and art-world roots were a direct model for their guitar approach.
The Stooges' raw, repetitive power fed their heavier songs, and they covered Stooges material.
Patti Smith's fusion of downtown poetry and rock informed their art-rock outlook.
Television's long, interlocking guitar lines influenced their extended twin-guitar passages.

cousins.why: Free-form playing that rejected standard harmony while keeping a strong pulse.
Experimental rock built on repetition and textural sound.

artists.name: Pixies
artists.summary: Pixies built songs on sudden shifts between quiet verses and loud, distorted choruses, with surf-tinged guitar and boy-girl vocals. That dynamic became a core template for 1990s alternative rock.
know: Surfer Rosa (1988) was recorded with engineer Steve Albini.
Their early records were released on the British label 4AD.
Kurt Cobain said he was trying to write a Pixies song when he wrote Smells Like Teen Spirit.

influencedBy.why: The band's ad seeking a bassist asked for fans of Hüsker Dü, and their melodic noise shaped the Pixies sound.
Joey Santiago has cited Hendrix, and his noisy, inventive lead lines show it.
Black Francis's raw, screaming delivery and the band's blunt power echo the Stooges.

cousins.why: Surreal, off-kilter songs with jagged guitar.
Playful, strange rock that mixes sweetness with noise.

artists.name: The Jesus and Mary Chain
artists.summary: The Jesus and Mary Chain set sweet 1960s pop melodies inside sheets of guitar feedback over simple, booming drums. Their debut Psychocandy laid the groundwork for shoegaze and noise pop.
know: The band is led by brothers Jim and William Reid.
Their first single, Upside Down, was released on Creation Records in 1984.
Just Like Honey opens with the drum pattern from the Ronettes' Be My Baby.

influencedBy.why: They built songs on Phil Spector's girl-group drums and melodies, quoting Be My Baby directly.
The Velvets' mix of drone, feedback and simple melody is the core of their sound.
The Reids have named the Beach Boys among the melodic pop sources under their noise.
The Stooges' raw, distorted minimalism shaped their abrasive early live sound.

cousins.why: Dreamy, retro pop melodies set in a dark, hazy atmosphere.
Vintage melodies and sounds wrapped in heavy, shadowy textures.

artists.name: My Bloody Valentine
artists.summary: My Bloody Valentine turned layered, pitch-bending guitars into a blurred wall of sound with soft vocals sunk into the mix. Loveless became the defining shoegaze album and a landmark in guitar texture and production.
know: Kevin Shields developed a glide guitar technique, strumming while working the tremolo arm.
Loveless (1991) was recorded across many studios over roughly two years.
Their third album, m b v, arrived in 2013, twenty-two years after Loveless.

influencedBy.why: The Mary Chain's mix of pop melody and feedback helped push them toward their noisier sound.
Sonic Youth's alternate tunings and guitar noise were an important model for Shields's experiments.
Shields has credited the Ramones' wall of simple, strummed guitar as a key early influence.

cousins.why: Music where texture and atmosphere matter more than individual parts.
Hazy, blurred production that buries voices inside the sound.

artists.name: The Stone Roses
artists.summary: The Stone Roses mixed 1960s jangle and psychedelic melody with loose, funky drumming influenced by dance club culture. They led the Madchester scene and paved the way for Britpop.
know: Their 1989 debut was produced by John Leckie.
Fools Gold paired a funk breakbeat with wah-wah guitar and became a dance-floor hit.
Reni's fluid, swinging drumming set them apart from other guitar bands of the time.

influencedBy.why: John Squire's ringing, melodic guitar draws on the Byrds' 1960s jangle.
Their harmonies and psychedelic pop arrangements echo the mid-period Beatles.
Squire and Ian Brown have cited the Clash as the band that inspired them to start playing.
Squire's wah-heavy lead playing on Fools Gold and Second Coming recalls Hendrix.

cousins.why: Music that bridged guitar psychedelia and dance-floor beats.
A melodic psychedelic band at the center of a youth scene.

artists.name: Red Hot Chili Peppers
artists.summary: Red Hot Chili Peppers fused slap-bass funk, punk energy and rhythmic vocals, later adding melodic, guitar-driven ballads. They became one of the most successful bands of the alternative era.
know: George Clinton produced their second album, Freaky Styley (1985).
Rick Rubin produced Blood Sugar Sex Magik (1991) and many later albums.
They were inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame in 2012.

influencedBy.why: They idolized P-Funk, and George Clinton produced Freaky Styley.
They covered Hendrix's Fire, and John Frusciante has named Hendrix as a major guitar influence.
Their hit cover of Higher Ground shows their debt to Wonder's funk.
Flea's slap-bass style follows the thumb-slapping technique of Sly's bassist Larry Graham.
Their tight, syncopated New Orleans funk grooves were a model for the band's rhythm section.
Flea and the band came up in the LA punk scene and have cited bands like Black Flag for their energy.

cousins.why: Heavy guitar riffs locked to funk grooves and rhythmic vocals.
A band that mixed punk energy, rap vocals and funk.

artists.name: Iron Maiden
artists.summary: Iron Maiden combined galloping bass lines, harmonized twin guitars and long, multi-part song structures, setting the melodic and epic standard for heavy metal in the 1980s.
genres: new wave of British heavy metal
know: Founder and bassist Steve Harris wrote much of the material and drives the band's galloping rhythm.
The Number of the Beast (1982), their first album with singer Bruce Dickinson, was their first UK No. 1.
They built a large global following largely through constant touring with little radio support.

influencedBy.why: Steve Harris has named Deep Purple as a key early influence, and Bruce Dickinson has cited Ian Gillan as a model for his singing.
Harris often credits early Genesis for his love of long songs with changing sections, a direct root of Maiden's epics.
Progressive rock bands like Yes informed Harris's interest in complex arrangements and melodic bass playing.
Guitarist Dave Murray has cited Hendrix as the player who made him take up guitar.
Priest's twin lead guitar format and non-blues metal sound preceded and paralleled Maiden's.

cousins.why: Long, multi-part songs with a virtuoso rhythm section at the center.
Big, theatrical arrangements and layered guitar harmonies.

artists.name: Metallica
artists.summary: Metallica fused the speed of Motörhead with the melody and structure of British heavy metal to help create thrash, then broadened into a mainstream hard rock band that became one of the biggest acts in the world.
know: Master of Puppets (1986) was the first metal recording added to the US National Recording Registry.
Their 1991 self-titled album, produced by Bob Rock, is one of the best-selling records of its era.
They were inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame in 2009.

influencedBy.why: Lars Ulrich was a devoted Motörhead fan and the band's speed and raw energy fed directly into early Metallica, who later recorded Motörhead covers.
Ulrich and James Hetfield have cited Maiden's twin guitar harmonies and long song structures as a model.
Hetfield has called Black Sabbath the root of heavy riffing and the band has performed Sabbath songs.
Seeing Deep Purple as a child is the experience Ulrich credits with getting him into hard rock.
Priest's fast, precise riffs and dual guitar parts are a widely noted part of Metallica's foundation.

cousins.why: Late 1980s hard rock band that went from underground grit to stadium scale.
Fast, aggressive underground music built on intensity and DIY touring.

artists.name: Slayer
artists.summary: Slayer played thrash at extreme tempos with chromatic, dissonant riffs and chaotic dueling solos, setting a new bar for speed and intensity that shaped death metal and other extreme styles.
know: Reign in Blood (1986), produced by Rick Rubin, packs ten songs into under 29 minutes.
Dave Lombardo's fast double-bass drumming became a reference point for extreme metal drummers.
Their 1996 album Undisputed Attitude consisted mostly of covers of punk and hardcore songs.

influencedBy.why: Slayer recorded a credited cover of Priest's Dissident Aggressor, and Priest's sharp twin guitar riffing shaped their early sound.
The early band played Maiden songs and adopted their galloping riffs and harmonized leads on Show No Mercy.
Slayer covered Minor Threat on Undisputed Attitude, and hardcore's speed fed Jeff Hanneman's riff writing.
They reworked the Stooges' I Wanna Be Your Dog on Undisputed Attitude, showing their debt to raw proto-punk.
Sabbath's ominous tritone-heavy riffing is a widely noted ancestor of Slayer's dark, chromatic style.

cousins.why: Pushed tempo and precision to the limit of what a rock band could play.
Abrasive, fast underground music that broke the rules of its scene.

artists.name: Megadeth
artists.summary: Megadeth played thrash with unusually intricate, fast riffing and technical lead guitar, pushing the genre toward precision and complexity.
know: Founder Dave Mustaine co-wrote several early Metallica songs before forming Megadeth.
Rust in Peace (1990), with guitarist Marty Friedman, is widely seen as a peak of technical thrash.
They won the 2017 Grammy for Best Metal Performance with Dystopia.

influencedBy.why: Motörhead's speed and aggression were part of the early thrash sound Mustaine helped build.
Priest's sharp twin guitar riffs and lead work are widely noted in Megadeth's style.
Maiden's melodic harmonized guitars informed Megadeth's dual lead passages.
Megadeth recorded a credited cover of Anarchy in the U.K., reflecting the punk energy in their playing.
The band covered Dixon's I Ain't Superstitious on Peace Sells, reworking a blues standard in a thrash setting.

cousins.why: Technically demanding rock built on precise, intricate playing.
Complex, tightly arranged guitar music led by a single strong-willed bandleader.

artists.name: Michael Jackson
artists.summary: Michael Jackson went from child lead singer of the Jackson 5 to the biggest pop star of the 1980s. Thriller is still regarded as the best-selling album of all time.
know: Thriller won a record eight Grammy Awards in a single night in 1984.
He first performed the moonwalk on television during 'Billie Jean' at Motown 25 in 1983.
His videos for 'Billie Jean' and 'Beat It' helped break MTV's color barrier.

influencedBy.why: Jackson named James Brown his greatest influence and copied his footwork and spins as a child.
Diana Ross was his Motown mentor, and he openly modeled parts of his singing and stage presence on her.
A Motown mentor and fellow child star who wrote 'I Can't Help It' for Off the Wall.
The Jackson 5 auditioned for Motown with Smokey's 'Who's Lovin' You', and Michael studied his phrasing.
The early Jackson 5 sound was built by Motown on Sly's funk-pop model, and Michael later bought Sly's publishing.
The Jacksons modeled their choreography and group vocals on Motown's leading male group.
Jackson cited Cooke's smooth tenor among the singers he studied.
He admired Lennon and McCartney's songwriting, recorded with McCartney and bought their catalog.
His socially aware later songs follow the path What's Going On opened at Motown.
The horn-driven disco-funk of Off the Wall sits squarely in Earth, Wind & Fire's lane.

cousins.why: The other singer-dancer who became the defining pop icon of his era.
A musician who became a worldwide symbol far beyond his genre.

artists.name: Madonna
artists.summary: Madonna built a career on constant reinvention, using club music, videos and provocation to become the best-selling female recording artist of all time.
know: She moved to New York in 1978 with little money to study dance.
Pepsi canceled her sponsorship deal in 1989 over the 'Like a Prayer' video.
Ray of Light (1998), made with William Orbit, won the Grammy for Best Pop Album.

influencedBy.why: Madonna has said her first concert, a Bowie show in Detroit, changed her life and showed her pop as theatre.
She has cited Debbie Harry as proof that a woman could front downtown New York pop on her own terms.
Madonna has said she worshipped Joni Mitchell as a teenager, especially Court and Spark.
Nile Rodgers produced Like a Virgin and brought Chic's dance-floor discipline to her sound.
She has named Diana Ross and Motown girl groups among her earliest pop models.
Her early club records follow the path Summer's disco hits opened for female dance stars.

cousins.why: A restless reinventor who treats each album as a new visual and sonic identity.
Club-rooted 1980s music that crossed from the dance floor to the charts.

artists.name: Whitney Houston
artists.summary: Whitney Houston's gospel-trained voice made her one of the most awarded artists of the 1980s and 1990s and set the standard for the pop power ballad.
know: Her mother is gospel singer Cissy Houston and Dionne Warwick is her cousin.
She had seven consecutive U.S. No. 1 singles from 1985 to 1988, a record.
The Bodyguard soundtrack (1992) is one of the best-selling albums of all time.
songs: I Wanna Dance with Somebody (Who Loves Me)

influencedBy.why: A close family friend whom Houston called a key influence on her gospel-to-pop singing.
Her biggest hit was a cover of Parton's 'I Will Always Love You', and Parton kept the writing credit.
Houston named Diana Ross as an early role model for a Black woman crossing over into pop stardom.

cousins.why: A big, controlled voice that defined the ballad in country music.
The gospel powerhouse whose church style shaped soul singing.

artists.name: Janet Jackson
artists.summary: The youngest Jackson sibling broke out with producers Jimmy Jam and Terry Lewis on Control and Rhythm Nation 1814, setting the template for choreographed, beat-driven R&B pop.
know: Rhythm Nation 1814 is the only album to produce No. 1 Hot 100 hits in three separate calendar years.
As a child she acted on Good Times and Diff'rent Strokes.
Control (1986) was made in Minneapolis with former members of Prince's side band the Time.

influencedBy.why: Her older brother's work set the bar for the video and dance-driven pop she built on.
She grew up around the family act and performed with her siblings as a child.
Jam and Lewis brought the Minneapolis funk sound they learned in Prince's orbit to her records.
'Got 'til It's Gone' samples Mitchell's 'Big Yellow Taxi' with Mitchell's approval and credit.

cousins.why: A dance-video innovator who made beat-driven music with striking choreography.
1980s electronic records with hard, programmed rhythms and dark undertones.

artists.name: George Michael
artists.summary: George Michael wrote and produced Wham!'s hits and then made Faith, becoming one of the most gifted soul-influenced pop songwriters of the 1980s.
know: Faith (1987) won the Grammy for Album of the Year.
He wrote 'Careless Whisper' when he was 17.
Faith made him the first white solo artist to top Billboard's Black albums chart.

influencedBy.why: His teenage idol, with whom he later dueted on 'Don't Let the Sun Go Down on Me'.
Michael frequently named Stevie Wonder as a primary influence and covered his songs live.
He idolized Franklin and recorded the No. 1 duet 'I Knew You Were Waiting (For Me)' with her.
He cited Freddie Mercury as an influence and sang 'Somebody to Love' at the Mercury tribute concert.
Bowie's genre-crossing 1970s records were part of his musical upbringing.

cousins.why: Polished British pop of the 1980s that drew on Black music.
Sophisticated, jazz-tinged songcraft with obsessive studio polish.

artists.name: Prince
artists.summary: Prince wrote, produced and played most instruments on his records, fusing funk, rock, new wave and soul into the Minneapolis sound and one of the deepest catalogs in pop.
know: He was credited with playing 27 instruments on his debut album, For You.
Purple Rain won the Academy Award for Best Original Song Score.
He changed his name to an unpronounceable symbol in 1993 during a dispute with Warner Bros.

influencedBy.why: Prince cited James Brown as a primary influence and studied his band leadership and dance moves.
Prince's integrated, mixed-gender band and rock-funk fusion followed Sly's blueprint.
Prince called Mitchell a favorite, cited Court and Spark and name-checked her in 'The Ballad of Dorothy Parker'.
Prince said Carlos Santana influenced his guitar playing more than Hendrix.
His flamboyant lead guitar is widely compared to Hendrix's.
Wonder's self-produced, multi-instrumentalist albums were a model for Prince's approach.
Prince admired their horn-driven funk and drew on it in his early bands.
His synth-funk and cosmic grooves share P-Funk's DNA.
His sweet falsetto follows Mayfield's soulful high register.
Prince cited Little Richard's flamboyant, gender-bending stage persona.
The two admired each other, and Prince's jazz-funk ambitions drew on Davis.

cousins.why: A constantly shifting rock star who blurred gender and genre lines.
Funk-steeped hip-hop with flamboyant style and genre-hopping ambition.

artists.name: Afrika Bambaataa
artists.summary: Bronx DJ and organizer whose 'Planet Rock' fused German synth-pop with funk and launched electro. He also founded the Universal Zulu Nation.
know: 'Planet Rock' (1982) borrows Kraftwerk's 'Trans-Europe Express' melody over a Roland TR-808 beat.
He founded the Universal Zulu Nation, an organization built around hip hop culture.
He recorded 'Unity' with James Brown in 1984.

influencedBy.why: 'Planet Rock' lifts Kraftwerk's 'Trans-Europe Express' melody and 'Numbers' rhythm.
He played James Brown records constantly and later recorded 'Unity' with him.
P-Funk's cosmic funk shaped his sound and his Soulsonic Force image.
He was known for playing YMO records in his DJ sets, part of his electro palette.
Sly's records were staples of his sets and his message of unity.
He followed Herc's lead in building parties around breaks.

cousins.why: Another early builder of electro who took Kraftwerk into Black American dance music.
A bandleader who tied dance music to a pan-African message.

artists.name: Run-DMC
artists.summary: Queens trio that stripped rap down to hard drums and shouted rhymes, and took it into the rock mainstream.
know: Their 1984 debut was the first rap album certified gold.
'Raising Hell' (1986) was the first rap album to go multi-platinum.
'My Adidas' led to an endorsement deal with Adidas.

influencedBy.why: They remade 'Walk This Way' with Steven Tyler and Joe Perry, joining rap and rock.
They grew up on the Bronx pioneers and pushed their style into a harder sound.
Their records are built on the break-based approach Herc started.

cousins.why: A blunt, stripped-down group that dressed the part and simplified their genre.
Loud, minimal and built on drums and riffs.

artists.name: LL Cool J
artists.summary: Rapper who was Def Jam's first star and showed rap could have both tough battle songs and love ballads.
know: 'Radio' (1985) was the first full-length album released by Def Jam.
'I Need Love' was one of the first rap ballads to top the R&B chart.
In 2017 he became the first rapper given a Kennedy Center Honor.
songs: I Can't Live Without My Radio

influencedBy.why: He has said hearing 'Rapper's Delight' made him want to rap.
He came up idolizing the Furious Five, especially Melle Mel.
He shared Run-DMC's label circle and their hard, drum-heavy approach.

cousins.why: A good-looking star who made a rough new sound into a teen idol phenomenon.
Built a career on smooth love songs aimed at women.

artists.name: Beastie Boys
artists.summary: Three New York punks who became a rap group, made the first No. 1 rap album and then reinvented themselves with sample collages and live instruments.
know: They started as a hardcore punk band in 1981.
'Licensed to Ill' (1986) was the first rap album to top the Billboard 200.
The group ended after Adam Yauch died in 2012.
songs: (You Gotta) Fight for Your Right (To Party!)

influencedBy.why: They toured with Run-DMC and shared producer Rick Rubin while moving into rap.
Bad Brains drove their teenage hardcore punk years.
'Rhymin & Stealin' is built on the drums of 'When the Levee Breaks.'
'Paul's Boutique' samples several Beatles songs, most clearly on 'The Sounds of Science.'
'Shadrach' is built on Sly's 'Loose Booty.'

cousins.why: A punk-rooted party band that grew into a more serious one.
Punks who soaked up hip hop and dub.

artists.name: Eric B. & Rakim
artists.summary: Duo of DJ Eric B. and rapper Rakim, whose calm, intricate rhyming changed how rappers wrote and delivered verses.
know: Rakim's internal rhymes and relaxed delivery replaced the shouted style of early rap.
Rakim has said he modeled his phrasing on John Coltrane's saxophone.
Coldcut's remix of 'Paid in Full' was a hit in the UK in 1987.

influencedBy.why: Rakim played saxophone and said he approached rhyme like Coltrane approached solos.
Their beats lean heavily on James Brown camp records, like Bobby Byrd's 'I Know You Got Soul.'

cousins.why: Changed what a soloist could do with rhythm and phrasing.
Redefined technique on his instrument for everyone after him.

artists.name: Boogie Down Productions
artists.summary: Bronx group led by KRS-One that moved from street records to teaching-style rap after DJ Scott La Rock was killed.
know: Co-founder Scott La Rock was shot dead in 1987, months after 'Criminal Minded' came out.
'The Bridge Is Over' was a key shot in the Bridge Wars against Queensbridge's Juice Crew.
KRS-One led the Stop the Violence Movement and its 1989 single 'Self Destruction.'
keyAlbums: Ghetto Music: The Blueprint of Hip Hop

influencedBy.why: Their early beats draw on James Brown funk breaks.
'South Bronx' lays out the Bronx origin story with Herc at its center.
'The Bridge Is Over' borrows the piano line of 'It's Still Rock and Roll to Me.'
'Dope Beat' samples 'Back in Black.'

cousins.why: A teacher-preacher figure whose songs carried a political lesson.
Political, confrontational and openly preachy about it.

artists.name: Public Enemy
artists.summary: Long Island group led by Chuck D and Flavor Flav whose dense, noisy production and political lyrics made them hip hop's most confrontational band.
know: Their production team, the Bomb Squad, layered dozens of samples into single tracks.
'Fight the Power' was written for Spike Lee's 'Do the Right Thing' (1989).
They were inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame in 2013.
keyAlbums: It Takes a Nation of Millions to Hold Us Back

influencedBy.why: James Brown samples run all through their records, and 'Fight the Power' borrows his grooves and shouts.
Chuck D has credited Run-DMC with making hard, rock-sized rap possible.
Their political rap follows the path of Scott-Heron's spoken-word protest.
'Black Steel in the Hour of Chaos' is built on an Isaac Hayes sample.
'She Watch Channel Zero?!' samples Slayer's 'Angel of Death.'

cousins.why: The political standard-bearers of their genre.
Loud political music aimed at the system.

artists.name: N.W.A
artists.summary: Compton group of Eazy-E, Ice Cube, Dr. Dre, MC Ren and DJ Yella that put West Coast gangsta rap on the map and drew fights with police and censors.
know: An FBI official sent a warning letter to their label over 'Fuck tha Police' in 1989.
'Straight Outta Compton' went platinum with almost no radio play.
They were inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame in 2016.

influencedBy.why: Their loud, dense production and anti-police stance took cues from Public Enemy.
Run-DMC's hard drum-machine sound was the starting point for their beats.
Dre's funk samples point toward the P-Funk sound he later built G-funk on.
James Brown breaks are all over their early tracks.

cousins.why: Shocked the establishment and drew censors and police attention.
Los Angeles band known for its battles with the LAPD.

artists.name: De La Soul
artists.summary: Long Island trio whose playful, sample-packed debut with producer Prince Paul opened up a gentler, stranger side of rap.
know: '3 Feet High and Rising' was produced by Prince Paul.
They were sued by the Turtles over a sample, a landmark case in sample clearance.
Their catalog was off streaming services until 2023 because of sample rights.

influencedBy.why: 'Me Myself and I' is built on Funkadelic's '(Not Just) Knee Deep.'
Dilla produced the title track of 'Stakes Is High.'
'Eye Know' samples Steely Dan's 'Peg.'
'Eye Know' uses the whistle from 'Sittin' On the Dock of the Bay.'
'The Magic Number' samples 'Five Feet High and Rising,' which also inspired the album title.
Their Native Tongues circle grew out of the Zulu Nation scene.

cousins.why: Art-school weirdness that still made people dance.
Built whole worlds out of playful sample collage.

artists.name: Slick Rick
artists.summary: London-born Bronx rapper with a British accent and an eyepatch whose story songs are some of the most quoted verses in hip hop.
know: He was born in London and moved to the Bronx as a child.
'La Di Da Di' with Doug E. Fresh is one of the most sampled and interpolated songs in hip hop.
He lost the sight in his right eye in a childhood accident, hence the eyepatch.
keyAlbums: The Great Adventures of Slick Rick

cousins.why: Very British character sketches told with humor.
Narrative songs about crime and consequences.

artists.name: Frankie Knuckles
artists.summary: DJ and producer known as the Godfather of House. His sets at Chicago's Warehouse club gave house music its name.
know: House music is named after the Warehouse, the Chicago club where he was resident DJ from 1977.
He won the first Grammy for Remixer of the Year, Non-Classical, in 1997.
Chicago named a street after him and declared August 25 Frankie Knuckles Day.

influencedBy.why: The disco records he played at the Warehouse, led by groups like Chic, were the raw material of house.
Moroder's drum-machine disco pointed toward the electronic sound house adopted.
Donna Summer's extended disco tracks were the long-form dance music his sets grew from.

cousins.why: A DJ whose parties launched a whole genre.
A DJ who turned mixing into an art.

artists.name: Juan Atkins
artists.summary: Detroit producer often called the originator of techno. With Cybotron and Model 500 he turned the futurism of Kraftwerk and funk into a new genre.
know: He is one of the Belleville Three with Derrick May and Kevin Saunderson.
He formed Cybotron with Rick Davis in the early 1980s.
He founded the Metroplex label in 1985.

influencedBy.why: Atkins has repeatedly named Kraftwerk as the spark for his electronic music.
P-Funk's space-age funk is a core part of his sound and Detroit techno's mythology.
YMO's electropop was part of the synth music heard on Detroit radio that shaped him.
Moroder's sequenced synth disco was another blueprint for machine-made dance music.

cousins.why: Turned Kraftwerk into Black dance music.
A Detroit producer who rebuilt a genre's rhythm.

artists.name: Depeche Mode
artists.summary: English band that grew from bright synth-pop into dark, stadium-sized electronic rock. They are one of the most successful electronic acts ever.
know: Vince Clarke wrote their early hits, then left after the first album.
Martin Gore became their main songwriter.
They were inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame in 2020.

influencedBy.why: Their early all-synth sound came straight from Kraftwerk's example.
Singer Dave Gahan has often named Bowie as his biggest influence.

cousins.why: Gloomy, romantic music with a huge fan base.
Dark electronic rock.

artists.name: R.L. Burnside
artists.summary: A North Mississippi hill country bluesman whose droning, trance-like grooves found a new audience in the 1990s. His Fat Possum records connected raw juke-joint blues with indie and punk fans.
know: He recorded for Fat Possum Records in the 1990s.
His neighbor Mississippi Fred McDowell taught him guitar.
He toured and recorded with the Jon Spencer Blues Explosion.

influencedBy.why: Named Hooker's boogie records as an early inspiration for his driving style.
Spent time around Muddy in Chicago and cited him as a hero.

cousins.why: Fuzzy, repetitive garage blues that grew from his records.
Hypnotic, looping grooves meant to entrance.

artists.name: Garth Brooks
artists.summary: The best-selling solo artist in US history by album sales, who brought rock-style arena shows to country in the 1990s.
know: He has said hearing George Strait's "Unwound" made him want to be a country singer.
Ropin' the Wind (1991) was the first country album to debut at number one on the Billboard 200.
In 1999 he released an album as an alter ego named Chris Gaines.
songs: Much Too Young (To Feel This Damn Old)

influencedBy.why: He has said hearing Strait's "Unwound" in 1981 made him choose country.
He often names James Taylor as his favorite singer-songwriter.
He cites KISS for his arena showmanship and covered "Hard Luck Woman" with them.
He had a hit covering Joel's "Shameless."
Haggard was among the traditional country singers he studied.

cousins.why: A stadium performer who connects with everyday fans.
Turned huge arena shows into a spectacle.

artists.name: Shania Twain
artists.summary: Canadian singer who fused country with big pop rock production and became one of the best-selling female artists ever.
know: Come On Over (1997) is the best-selling album by a female country artist.
Her albums were produced by her then husband Robert John "Mutt" Lange.
Lyme disease damaged her voice and kept her off stage for years.
songs: Man! I Feel Like a Woman!

influencedBy.why: She has named Dolly Parton as a key influence growing up.

cousins.why: A pop superstar who controlled her image and broke barriers.
A crossover star who brought her genre to a global pop audience.

artists.name: Alison Krauss
artists.summary: Fiddler and singer whose clear voice brought bluegrass to a wide audience. She is one of the most awarded artists in Grammy history.
know: She was a child fiddle contest champion before signing to Rounder at 14.
Raising Sand, with Robert Plant, won the Grammy for Album of the Year in 2009.
She sang on the O Brother, Where Art Thou? soundtrack.
keyAlbums: Now That I've Found You: A Collection
songs: When You Say Nothing at All
Down to the River to Pray

influencedBy.why: Her band Union Station plays in the bluegrass tradition Monroe created.
She collaborated with Robert Plant on Raising Sand and its follow-up.

cousins.why: A soft, pure voice that crosses over to a broad audience.
Flawless tone and control.

artists.name: The Chicks
artists.summary: Trio of Natalie Maines, Martie Maguire and Emily Strayer who blended bluegrass instruments with pop country and became the best-selling female group in country.
know: Country radio blacklisted them after Maines criticized President George W. Bush in 2003.
Taking the Long Way won five Grammys, including Album of the Year.
They dropped "Dixie" from their name in 2020.

influencedBy.why: They had a hit with their cover of "Landslide."
Their banjo, fiddle and dobro come from the bluegrass tradition.

cousins.why: Best-selling women's group that spoke its mind.
A dominant female group.

artists.name: Elliott Smith
artists.summary: Singer-songwriter whose whispered vocals and intricate guitar songs set the standard for sad, intimate indie folk.
know: "Miss Misery" was nominated for an Oscar, and he performed it at the 1998 ceremony.
He first played in the Portland band Heatmiser.
He died in 2003 at age 34.

influencedBy.why: He often named the Beatles as his biggest influence and covered their songs live.
He covered Big Star's "Thirteen."
His soft, intricate guitar songs follow the Nick Drake model.

cousins.why: A fragile, revered voice who died young.
Intimate, introspective, emotionally raw songs.

artists.name: Jeff Buckley
artists.summary: Jeff Buckley had a wide-ranging voice and made one studio album, Grace, before drowning at 30. His version of Leonard Cohen's Hallelujah became the best-known recording of the song.
know: His father was folk singer Tim Buckley.
He drowned in the Wolf River in Memphis in 1997.
He built his following playing solo at the New York cafe Sin-é.
keyAlbums: Sketches for My Sweetheart the Drunk

influencedBy.why: His cover of Cohen's Hallelujah is his best-known recording.
He named Led Zeppelin's Physical Graffiti as one of the first records that hooked him.
He covered Lilac Wine on Grace after hearing Nina Simone's version.
He named Billie Holiday among the singers who shaped his phrasing.
He covered the Smiths' I Know It's Over in concert.
He covered Dylan's If You See Her, Say Hello on Live at Sin-é.
He covered Big Star's Kanga Roo on Grace-era releases.

cousins.why: Both pair a soaring falsetto with dramatic, layered rock.
Both use a fragile high voice to carry raw emotion.

artists.name: The Black Crowes
artists.summary: The Black Crowes, led by brothers Chris and Rich Robinson, revived early 1970s Stones- and Faces-style rock in the grunge era. Their debut sold millions.
know: Their cover of Otis Redding's Hard to Handle was their breakout hit.
They toured with Jimmy Page in 2000, playing Led Zeppelin songs.
The Robinson brothers have split and reunited several times.
keyAlbums: The Southern Harmony and Musical Companion

influencedBy.why: Their breakout hit was a cover of Otis Redding's Hard to Handle.
Their loose, bluesy rock is modeled on early 1970s Rolling Stones.
Their long jams and Southern roots follow the Allman Brothers.
They backed Jimmy Page on a 2000 tour of Led Zeppelin songs, released as Live at the Greek.

cousins.why: Both revive a classic sound with real feel instead of nostalgia.
Both are Southern retro-rooted acts with a rock edge.

artists.name: Nirvana
artists.summary: Nirvana fused punk noise with pop melody and carried underground rock into the mainstream with Nevermind in 1991.
know: Nevermind replaced Michael Jackson's Dangerous at number one on the Billboard 200 in January 1992.
Their debut Bleach was released on the Seattle label Sub Pop in 1989.
Their MTV Unplugged in New York set leaned on covers and won a Grammy for Best Alternative Music Album.

influencedBy.why: Kurt Cobain said he was trying to write a Pixies song with Smells Like Teen Spirit and borrowed their quiet verse, loud chorus dynamic.

Cobain cited Black Flag's slow, heavy side as a model for Nirvana's early sludgy punk.
Cobain championed Sonic Youth, whose move to DGC helped steer Nirvana to the same label.
Cobain listed Raw Power among his favorite records and drew on its raw guitar attack.
Nirvana closed their Unplugged set with Lead Belly's arrangement of Where Did You Sleep Last Night.
